#1659. Opinion: One of the best young players in the world is coming to Liverpool

Whether in January or in the summer one of the best young players in the world is going to be heading to Liverpool.

Julian Ward has an enormous task on his hands at Liverpool, but there's also a genuine sense of excitement about what he's trying to build at Anfield.

The Reds are clearly looking towards the future. Ward wants to assemble a squad capable of dominating English and European football for years to come.

Essentially, he's trying to build Liverpool's next super team.

And when you look at some of the young players already at the club, there's plenty of reason to be optimistic.

Rio Ngumoha looks like a generational talent. Trey Nyoni is developing into an outstanding midfielder, while the likes of Florian Wirtz, Jeremy Jacquet and Bradley Barcola could become cornerstones of the team for the next decade.

Behind them, Liverpool have an academy packed with exciting prospects who could eventually make the step up.

Why Julian Ward needs time to achieve success with LiverpoolLiverpool supporters will understandably want immediate success, especially after watching the club struggle over the last few seasons. However, rebuilding a team isn't straightforward. There are still glaring weaknesses in the squad. Liverpool need a specialist holding midfielder, a natural right-winger and greater defensive depth. Questions also remain over the long-term futures of several experienced players. Ward cannot solve every problem in a single transfer window. Nor can Andoni Iraola be expected to transform this young squad into Premier League and Champions League winners overnight. These things take time. Just look at how Jurgen Klopp gradually assembled his great Liverpool side. It required several transfer windows, difficult decisions and plenty of patience before everything finally clicked. Ward will be hoping to follow a similar blueprint.

#1658. Norway vs Wales - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matt Law | 12 Nov 2026 15:18, Last updated: 12 Nov 2026 15:22

Two teams still in with a chance of making the quarter-finals of the 2026-27 UEFA Nations League will lock horns on Saturday, with Norway hosting Wales.

Norway have actually lost each of their last three matches in Group A4 to give themselves a mountain to climb, while Wales have been beaten in three of their four games in the competition, but qualification for the final four is still possible at this stage.

Norway have a record of one win and three defeats from their four matches in Group A4, with three points leaving them at the bottom of the section on three points.

The Red, White and Blues are fourth but are level on points with third-placed Wales and only three points behind second-placed Denmark, so it is still all to play for ahead of the final two matchdays in the group stage.

Stale Solbakken's side opened their Group A4 campaign with a 3-2 success over Denmark, but they have lost twice to Portugal and also to Wales in their last three games.

Norway need to beat both Wales and Denmark, and a victory over the latter would be especially important, as they would then lead the head-to-head tie-breaker, which could potentially be crucial when it comes to the final positions in the section.

National Team are competing in League A of the Nations League for the first time, so they are bidding to secure what would be a first-ever quarter-final position.

Wales' route into the quarter-finals of the tournament is more complicated given that they have lost both games against Denmark, who therefore have the advantage in any head-to-head tiebreaker, which might be crucial after all of the fixtures have taken place.

Craig Bellamy's side had a difficult start to their Group A4 campaign, suffering back-to-back defeats to Portugal and Denmark at the end of September.

The Dragons then managed to post a 2-1 victory over Norway in their opening match of October, but they suffered a 1-0 loss to Denmark last time out.

Wales could join Denmark on six points with a win in this game, depending on what occurs between the Danes and Portugal, which would put them in a position to claim a top-two spot, but so much could still happen before the end of the section.

The Dragons have faced Norway on 12 occasions, boasting a record of four wins, four draws and four defeats, and they have actually been victorious in each of the last three matches between the two sides.

Norway have four players who are one booking away from missing the team's next match, including Martin Odegaard.

There are not expected to be any major surprises in the Norway side for this match, with Oscar Bobb and Antonio Nusa both expected to feature in the final third of the field.

Erling Haaland, meanwhile, is in line to win his 60th cap, and the striker will be looking to add to the 65 goals that he has scored for his country.

As for Wales, Benjamin Cabango and Sorba Thomas are both out of the match through suspension, while six other players are one booking away from being banned for the team's next fixture, including Ethan Ampadu.

Harry Wilson missed the team's last international period through injury, but the 29-year-old is available here and is set to start, while Daniel James could have a role through the middle against Norway.

Chris Mepham and Rubin Colwill are also potentially in line for starts on Saturday.

Selvik; Ryerson, Ajer, Ostigard, Wolfe; Odegaard, Berge, Berg; Bobb, Haaland, Nusa

Ward; N Williams, Mepham, Davies, Dasilva; Ampadu, R Colwill; Johnson, Cullen, Wilson; D James

Norway have struggled in the section so far, but we are expecting Haaland to help the hosts secure a vital three points on Saturday.

#1657. Tottenham are proof that a truckload of NFL and Beyonce cash is no use if you don't spend it properly, writes TOM COLLOMOSSE - after Roberto De Zerbi's £500m team saw their mini-revival ended by Leeds

Published: 09:34 EST, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 11:04 EST, 7 November 2026

Clubs outside European football’s elite are convinced the game’s financial rules are rigged to protect the richest and keep out the pretenders.

But Tottenham are living proof that making a truckload of money from Beyonce concerts and NFL fixtures is no use if you do not spend it properly.

A decade ago, Spurs fans complained frequently that Daniel Levy would not loosen the purse strings. At the time, the club was riding high under Mauricio Pochettino but could not take the final jump that – perhaps – a world-class signing or two would have delivered.

On reflection, perhaps the hierarchy were right back then. Maybe if they had worked within tighter limits in recent years, they might have made more sensible decisions in the market.

Tottenham’s starting XI at Leeds cost the best part of £500million with Leeds’ barely a quarter of that. It did not stop substitute Noah Okafor settling a tight game late in the second half and ending Spurs’ mini-revival.

Consider Pochettino’s Tottenham side at its peak. We’re not talking just Harry Kane, but Mousa Dembele, Kyle Walker, Christian Eriksen and Danny Rose. Hugo Lloris, Jan Vertonghen, Toby Alderweireld, Dele Alli and Heung-min Son.

Not many of the current crop would make it anywhere that team which is rather worrying when we consider the sums Tottenham have invested.

Leeds United leapfrogged Tottenham into the top half of the Premier League table

Roberto De Zerbi saw his side's three-game winning run come to an end at Elland Road

The problem with this squad is that they have a whole heap of players in the ‘good-to-very good’ bracket, who are largely interchangeable among themselves. A few, like Micky van de Ven, James Maddison, Sandro Tonali and potentially Mateus Fernandes, are a little above that category. There is nobody, though, who you could truly call world class.

Take Roberto De Zerbi, too. A bright, talented boss who did commendable work at Sassuolo, Shakhtar Donetsk, Brighton and Marseille. He does not, however, belong to the top rank like Pep Guardiola, Luis Enrique, Unai Emery or – increasingly – Mikel Arteta.

Here, Okafor scored the only goal barely a minute after coming on, combining with fellow sub Harry Wilson and slotting beyond Antonin Kinsky. Leeds made most of the chances in the second half and ended a five-match run without a win, though James Trafford saved Jan Paul van Hecke’s header late on to preserve the points.

Spurs have enough talent to keep them well clear of relegation and it is the kind of squad who can make a strong cup run. That is what Spurs have often been in modern times and there is nothing essentially wrong with it. Given the cash the current regime have splashed, though, they may just expect a little more.

Every summer, they do it. They tweak, fiddle and fuss. They preach about high bars, mic up officials and apologise to angry managers.

They have even changed the name of their organisation from PGMOL to Pro Ref, but they will never remove the controversy that VAR causes nearly every weekend.

Towards the end of the first half, Mathys Tel screamed in pain after Jayden Bogle fouled him. Replays showed Bogle’s studs make a solid contact with the Frenchman’s ankle but after nearly five minutes of checking, referee John Brooks was told to stick with his original decision.

‘Jayden is one of the fairest players in the country,’ said Leeds boss Daniel Farke. ‘He is more like a butterfly than an eagle and he would not even foul a player on purpose, let alone injure them. It was never intentional and maybe this is why the VAR said it was not a red card.’

Bogle escaped because there was ‘a lack of speed going into the challenge’ which VAR Tony Harrington deemed ‘reckless’ rather than dangerous. Whatever it was, Tel was injured moments later and Leeds had got away with one. Tel will have scans and De Zerbi fears the worst.

In real time, it looked a standard foul. After re-watching, though, it was hard to see how Bogle could stay on the pitch.

For all the decisions VAR overturns correctly, there are still far too many that leave too many people baffled.

‘I can’t say more as I didn’t see the situation clearly but I was surprised to see Pedro Porro given a yellow card in the second half for a foul in a similar position,’ said De Zerbi. ‘I don’t know if [Bogle’s] foul should be a red card or not but today the parameters of the referee were not good enough for these situations.’

Leeds are planning to expand Elland Road, but the stadium must not lose its raw essence

Leeds are working to increase the size of Elland Road and hope that the capacity will eventually be 53,000. Whatever they do, they must not damage the place’s raw essence.

Only Arsenal, Manchester City and Liverpool have a better points-per-game record than Leeds since Daniel Farke became boss in 2023. The lunchtime kick-off will never match the floodlit fixture for atmosphere but the second half here was as raucous as on its best days, and the stadium shook when Okafor slotted the winner past Antonin Kinsky.

‘When you have a few games without the winning feeling, it’s always difficult,’ Farke admitted. ‘Heading into the international break, it’s important to win again.’

There is plenty to improve for Leeds. If Dominic Calvert-Lewin catches a cold, where do the goals come from? Who can replace what Ethan Ampadu provides in the centre of midfield?

These are questions for Farke to tackle but with Elland Road at his team’s back, he has solid foundations on which to build.

Leeds (3-5-2): Trafford 6; Justin 7, Elvedi 7, MUHAREMOVIC 8; Bogle 7 (Rodon 90+3), Longstaff 6 (Gruev 90+2), Ampadu 7, Tanaka 6 (Wilson 77), Gudmundsson 7 (Bard 46, 7); Calvert-Lewin 7, Nmecha 6 (Okafor 77).

Tottenham (4-2-3-1): Kinsky 7; Porro 6 (Gallagher 65, 6), Van Hecke 7, Van de Ven 7, Robertson 6; Fernandes 6 (Bentancur 65, 6), Tonali 7; Kudus 6 (Williams-Barnett 83), Gray 6, Tel 6 (Solanke 43, 6); Marmoush 5 (Kulusevski 65, 6).

#1656. Opinion: He's incredible, Liverpool have found the next Khvicha Kvaratskhelia

Liverpool have found their next Kvicha Kvaratskhelia, and he's incredible.

Liverpool are entering a new era under Julian Ward, and it's becoming increasingly clear that the club's transfer strategy is undergoing a significant transformation.

For years, the Reds built their success around identifying undervalued players who were ready to make an immediate impact.

Think Mohamed Salah, Sadio Mane, Andy Robertson and Georginio Wijnaldum. Players who arrived at Anfield with something to prove and developed into world-class stars.

But now, Ward appears determined to take things in a slightly different direction.

Rather than waiting for players to establish themselves at the highest level, Liverpool want to identify the next generation of superstars before they become household names.

And it's an approach that makes a lot of sense.

How Liverpool are building a team for the futureThe transfer market has become increasingly expensive. Even relatively unproven players are commanding enormous fees, and Liverpool simply cannot afford to compete financially with the likes of Manchester City and Real Madrid for every established superstar. Instead, the Reds are looking to get ahead of the competition. We've already seen the club become far more aggressive in recruiting young talent from across the world. The arrivals of Mor Talla Ndiaye, Ifeanyi Ndukwe, Samuel Martinez, Armin Pecsi and Lucca Brughmans are all examples of Liverpool investing in players with enormous potential. Meanwhile, the club's academy is already producing exciting talents like Rio Ngumoha, Trey Nyoni, Joshua Abe and Will Wright. The objective is simple. Liverpool want to build a conveyor belt of talent capable of sustaining success for the next decade.

#1655. Chelsea transfer news: Every Blues loan player ranked in minutes, quartet with less game time than Alejandro Garnacho

By Darren Plant | 12 Nov 2026 15:34, Last updated: 12 Nov 2026 15:35

When Chelsea were searching for loan destinations for a wide array of their fringe players and starlets during the summer transfer window, they found themselves undertaking an elaborate operation.

With 24 players going elsewhere on a temporary basis, it was inevitable that some deals would bring less success than others.

Remarkably, five of the players who have recently departed Stamford Bridge are yet to reach 100 minutes for their respective clubs.

In sharp contrast, two teenagers have accumulated over 1,000 minutes, emphasising the different experiences that the players in question are having.

Here, Sports Mole reveals the amount of minutes that each of their loan players have racked up between the start of the campaign and the November international break.

Chelsea chiefs are being rewarded for finding suitable EFL clubs for a number of their academy players.

Most notably, 17-year-old winger Ryan Kavuma-McQueen has reached 718 minutes across 14 games for Championship club Portsmouth.

With the teenager also starring in a well-performing side, there are encouraging signs that he can become a future Chelsea first-teamer.

The same applies to central midfielder Reggie Walsh, who has amassed 923 minutes across 14 games for League One outfit Wigan Athletic.

Left-back Ishe Samuels-Smith is also up to 803 minutes across 12 games for Notts County, finally kick-starting his career after a frustrating period at Swansea City in 2025-26.

Defender Kaiden Wilson sits at the top of Chelsea loan players minutes list with 1,431 minutes over 18 appearances for League Two team Rochdale.

Much is being made of Alejandro Garnacho's situation at Aston Villa, and rightly so. The Argentine has racked up just 95 minutes across seven substitute outings.

However, there are four players - Shim Mheuka, Dujuan Richards, Landon Emenalo and Mykhaylo Mudryk - who have played even less minutes than Garnacho.

Chelsea will be frustrated that Mheuka and Emenalo are not getting more chances at Celtic. Despite their general inconsistency, Mheuka is yet to make a single senior start for the Glasgow giants.

There is an argument that as many as 15 players will be satisfied with their current situations out on loan.

Mamadou Sarr's time at Real Sociedad is going under the radar, with the Senegal international now up to 778 minutes across 10 games for the Spanish club.

Dario Essugo is also impressing at Strasbourg, contributing two goals and one assist from his 458 minutes in central midfield.

However, Jesse Derry is a clear example of someone who may be recalled in January, providing that the agreement with Sporting Lisbon include a break clause.

Derry has accumulated just 133 minutes across seven games for the Portuguese giants. Chelsea may look to find a suitable Championship club for the second half of the campaign, which would free up a foreign loan spot in the process.

#1654. Floyd Samba’s Man City debut double has father Chris dancing

There was very much a Samba beat to this Manchester City victory – and it almost had a famous father in the crowd up dancing.

This was a night when Brazilian Allan Elias scored his first goal on an enterprising first appearance for City.

But it was another debutant who stole the show as the Carabao Cup holders sailed past Norwich City to set up a fourth-round meeting with Brighton.

Floyd Samba scored two fine goals and had a hand in another on a dream debut that had his beaming dad up off his seat and thrusting his arms in the air as if ready to party.

If the Samba surname feels familiar, that is because Floyd’s father Christopher played more than 200 games for Blackburn Rovers, Queens Park Rangers and Aston Villa.

In fact, it was very much a family affair as Floyd’s brothers Tyrone and Emerson, who are also in City’s academy and hoping one day to tread a similar path, joined in the jubilant celebrations alongside their mother, a visibly emotional Theresa.

This particular evening belonged to Floyd, though. Deployed as a lone striker by Enzo Maresca, you would not have known he ordinarily plays as a midfielder such was the confidence and composure the 17-year-old oozed.

Norwich could not live with him or City for that matter as Maresca’s impressive start as manager since replacing Pep Guardiola continued apace.

This must have been an incredibly satisfying moment for Samba Sr. He came through incredible hardship – at one stage as a teenager he was rough-sleeping – to forge an impressive career totalling more than 450 games for club and country.

So to be in a position to now have three sons in City’s academy and one produce a debut like this will fill him with enormous pride. Floyd was later seen enjoying a warm embrace with his dad in the crowd, moments after being congratulated by Tyrone, a year his senior, and 12-year-old Emerson, who plays for City’s Under-13s.

“I knew there would be an opportunity to get some minutes for the first time with the first team – to get a debut like that is mind blowing,” Samba said. “I couldn’t believe it myself, but that’s just the beginning, I’ve got a big career ahead of me. It was a great debut.”

Floyd caught the eye with a fine free-kick in City’s 2-1 FA Youth Cup final victory over Manchester United last season and now he has goals for the senior side to his name. Pretty stunning they were, too.

The first was a superbly steered header past two Norwich bodies on the line from Allan’s cross and the second a lovely, nonchalantly curled finish low into the far corner.

What a moment for Floyd Samba! 😍A goal on his Man City debut for the 17-year-old, son of former Blackburn defender Chris 🩵 pic.twitter.com/VCVfX9HCNn

Chris Samba has deliberately kept a low profile, keen to let his sons get on with their own careers free of distractions, but there was no chance he was going to be able to suppress his emotions in that instant. And nor should he. It was some moment for the boy and his family.

As impressed as Maresca was by the goals, it will have been other elements of Samba’s game that also caught the eye. He did extremely well to hold off the attentions of Norwich’s centre-backs when receiving a pass from Ayyoub Bouaddi and then returning the ball to the Moroccan who released Rayan Cherki through to score City’s second. His movement was also sharp, at one point taking a difficult pass sweetly in an adjusted strike, only for Norwich’s Bruno Alves to come across to make a timely intervention before Samba could get his shot off.

"Was there any doubt?"Ayyoub Bouaddi with his first assist for Man City as he sets up Rayan Cherki to make it 2-0 🔵 pic.twitter.com/0gfxp5GDXy

“It was satisfying not just for the two goals but for the entire performance,” Maresca said. “He didn’t play many games as a nine but he was good. He’s young, full of energy, strong, he can finish.”

Allan, a £34m summer signing from Palmeiras, will have been just as pleased with his contribution. Maresca’s fluid formation initially resembled a 3-1-5-1 with Allan effectively operating as a right wing-back but he stuck doggedly to the task before eventually getting the moment to showcase his quality, first with his cross for Samba and later with a neat solo run and finish.

Driving inside Sam Field and then cutting back inside the Norwich man before curling an inch perfect finish into the bottom corner – all of it done with his left foot – it was quite the introduction.

Allan on his debut! 🇧🇷Magic from the Brazilian to make it 3-0 to Man City 💥 pic.twitter.com/nw6lNqh1yL

Hugo Viana, City’s director of football, has said supporters will need to be patient with Allan and that it may take the 22-year-old time to adjust to English football but this first outing will do his confidence plenty of good.

“It was important for him to play 90 minutes and to see a little bit the English competition that is a bit different from South America so overall was good,” Maresca said.

Cherki was the only survivor from the team that started Sunday’s victory over Manchester United but it all felt pretty seamless from City. Bouaddi, the £85m signing from Lille, was poised and graceful in midfield alongside the impressive Mateo Kovacic and Geronimo Rulli could not have asked for a much quieter debut in goal.

FLOYD SAMBA again!! 🌟The 17-year-old curls one in to score his second on his Man City debut with his dad Christopher watching on in the stands 👏 pic.twitter.com/fJ5mfEWBx1

Nico O’Reilly looked like he had barely broken a sweat despite Norwich’s players routinely being unable to keep up with him. Norwich themselves made nine changes but the gulf in class was enormous and testament to City’s strength in depth.

The game also gave Maresca the opportunity to give run outs to two more academy graduates who played in that Youth Cup final triumph, Kaden Braithwaite and Ryan McAidoo and the latter got his own name on the scoresheet to make it 5-0.

All told there were seven City academy graduates on the pitch, two of them playing for Norwich. This was certainly a night to remember for the club’s youth production line.

With the dominant performance, Man City have earned themselves the privilege of hosting Brighton in the next round, who will no doubt prove a much stiffer challenge than Norwich. They become the sixth all-Premier League tie in the next round, with only Fleetwood, Bradford and Peterborough remaining from outside the top flight:

Erling Haaland left out of the squad, watching from the stands, would have enjoyed that performance from Floyd Samba. Here is his second goal for you to enjoy on his debut night:

FLOYD SAMBA again!! 🌟The 17-year-old curls one in to score his second on his Man City debut with his dad Christopher watching on in the stands 👏 pic.twitter.com/fJ5mfEWBx1

Five unanswered goals and a home-grown hero emerges for Manchester City!

Great through ball from O’Reilly, which Lewis lets run past him for the dummy. McAidoo runs on to it on the right of the box and first-time fires it low into the far corner.

It has been a perfect night for Manchester City’s academy.

Well we look like we’re heading for a matching scoreline to the previous edition of the fixture. That pesky shot on target is still eluding Norwich, whereas Samba is still out there looking for his hat-trick.

Two minutes of time to be added – who will get there first?

O’Reilly sends a high, looping ball to the back post from the left side, where McAidoo rushes to meet it but can’t get over it under pressure.

Final change for Norwich, as Kvistgaarden who has not had much service tonight, comes off for Schwartau.

Bouaddi sends a looping ball across the field to McAidoo, which he picks up on the edge of the box, but he is unable to get the ball under control to take his shot and it is cleared away as far as another City shirt.

The corner comes in to the centre of the box but is headed out by a City shirt.

It’s all slightly too little too late for Norwich.

They get another corner as Musaba tries to send a cross into the box from the right and it is blocked out.

A free-kick for Norwich now as O’Reilly commits the foul 35 yards out. It goes in towards McConville at the back post, but Ait-Nouri heads it out for a Norwich corner.

Mo Touré strays just offside on the edge of the box, as Musaba sends a lovely little ball over to find him on the turn and the forward slots it past Rulli. Celebrations don’t quite begin before the flag goes up but that is a shame for the visitors.

Norwich have managed to get more of a grip in this half, despite conceding two more goals, but they are still without a shot on goal as we approach the final 15 minutes.

Man City take off scorer of their third goal Allan to bring on Braithwaite.

Norwich replace Ben Slimane and Bruno Alves with Touré and McConville.

Samba again at the heart of the action, laying off the ball to McAidoo on the right for the winger to run into the box. His shot towards the far post is saved low by Grimshaw who spills it almost into the path of Lewis, but Norwich survive.

Lewis makes a run down the right-hand side and crosses into Samba on the edge of the box. He lays off to McAidoo, but his shot goes sailing over the bar.

A surprise to no one, it is chucking it down in Manchester.

Big cheers from the away end as Norwich get their first corner of the evening. It is lofted high and long to the back post, where it is headed away by Bouaddi. It bounces out to Musaba, who has just come on, and he strikes it from the top of the box on the half-volley.

His shot cuts through a crowd in the box and has Rulli diving to his left, but it goes wide of the post. What an introduction that would have been!

Well all the stories from this match will be all about young Floyd Samba. Feel free to leave your best punny Samba/dance-related headlines in the comments section.

For Man City as you would expect it is all about game management from here on out.

Some more changes to report for Norwich as well, as Crnac is replaced by Musaba.

Wright is able to run in to space towards the edge of the box, but as has been their story all evening, his pass out to the wing is just not where it needs to be and their effort just breaks down.

What a way to score a second! A night to remember for Floyd Samba!

Norwich try and play out from the back but far too sloppy and Ait-Nouri picks up the ball on the left of the box. He has plenty of time to tee up Samba inside the box at the left corner, who finds himself with plenty of space to curl his shot into the far corner, beating the diving Grimshaw.

We may be seeing plenty more of him this season.

Norwich looking for their way back into the game, as the ball comes down the left, fizzed in low and flashes past Rulli, trying to claim it. It deflects off a crowd of bodies and spins up, but Fisher can’t connect and it spins away harmlessly wide of the goal.

It is definitely Norwich’s best chance of the game and Fisher will be upset he hasn’t made more of that.

And Allan makes it three! Minutes after the restart, the Brazilian makes his own mark on his debut.

Maresca switched him onto the left side to escape Yongwa, and he picks up the ball outside the box and makes the run inside. He runs circles around Field and slots the ball home into the far bottom corner.

Some changes from both sides at half-time. McAidoo comes on for Cherki, though O’Reilly is the one to move up into midfield to fill the gap.

45 minutes left for the visitors to create something special!

What a moment for Floyd Samba! 😍A goal on his Man City debut for the 17-year-old, son of former Blackburn defender Chris 🩵 pic.twitter.com/VCVfX9HCNn

Manchester City will be the ones to host Brighton in the next round – giving the visitors the opportunity to pull off a remarkable feat of knocking out both Manchester sides should they win.

Enjoy the highlights from last night as they came from behind to dispatch Man Utd:

And without much ado at the end of the half, we have reached the break. City put themselves in control with two quick-fire goals and it looks a tall task for Norwich to find their way back into the match.

Credit where it is due, Yongwa has been very good for Norwich. He has stood fast, made some very good challenges and stopped Allan getting much of a look-in on the right.

As we approach half-time, the stats tell a sorry story. Norwich have had just 28% possession and created a single shot, none on target.

As City come again, Norwich have pulled every man back to try and keep the situation salvageable before the break.

Samba was in again there, making a run into the box with a ball from Cherki, wrestling with Bruno Alves as he goes. The defender does enough to throw him off and Grimshaw is able to come out and snatch the ball.

Man City are looking to close this out now, and they look threatening every time they break.

Ait-Nouri is the latest to try his luck, making a run into the box from the left, but his shot is blocked.

A few minutes to remember here for Floyd Samba. First he steers home a very well taken header to give City the lead and then he plays a crucial role in the second, holding the ball up well before laying it off to Bouaddi to release Cherki to score. That’s how to make an impression on your debut.

And the floodgates have opened. Two goals in two minutes for the defending champions.

Samba finds Bouaddi in midfield, who takes it forward and feeds Cherki running to his left. He gets himself one-on-one and slots cool as you like into the bottom left corner.

City are in control all of a sudden and Norwich will be devastated.

As soon as I say that, Floyd Samba finds a way through.

He has looked the brightest for City, and O’Reilly sends a cross over the box from the left, drawing Grimshaw away from position. The ball is pinged back in by Allan and the youngster stoops to meet it, heading in to the bottom corner.

Norwich have been very disciplined in defence so far. Yongwa has been closing down Allan on the wing very well.

Cherki is starting to get some momentum – but is swarmed by yellow shirts as he picks up the ball on the edge of the area.

Another loose ball from City in midfield and Norwich pick it up again. The ball to set the front line free is equally as loose from the visitors though and it breaks down once again.

Samba is looking lively, racing to get on a ball in front of Darling just on the edge of the box. Darling recovers to send it out for a corner, which becomes a free kick after Ait-Nouri wrestles his man to the ground at the back post as City are taking.

Wright sends a long ball across the field, looking for a man on the right side but Rulli is alert to it and comes to claim at the edge of the box.

Kovacic shows some promise with a strong run on the ball down the centre of the field, taking the ball all the way to the edge of the box, where he collides with a defender, and the ball spins away for Norwich to clear out.

This is better from City, who have looked like they’re lacking drive so far.

Yongwa again probing down the left side. It takes two to dispossess him and Man City manage to get the throw in, but approaching 20 minutes Norwich will be happy with this.

Kovacic loses the ball in midfield and Norwich surge forward. The move breaks down as Wright’s pass to Diallo on the wing is just behind him and he can’t take it forward into the box.

Spent the first 10 minutes trying to work out City’s system and settled on a 3-1-5-1, with Bouaddi operating as a nominal third centre-back, but it seems to have changed again now with O’Reilly dropping to left back and Bouaddi stepping into midfield. No doubt the metamorphosis will continue.

This Man City team have never played all together and it is clear that they’re still settling in here, figuring out how they’re going to press here.

Kovacic in the captain’s armband is tying it all together in midfield.

Khusanov threads a lovely ball to Samba who flicks it into the path of Lewis, who takes it and makes a run into the box. He creates space and sends a right-footed shot over the bar – but Man City are building.

Norwich make a move forward, with Yongwa bringing the ball down the left side but his cross into the box is blocked by Allan sliding in. The Brazilian is then fouled again as Yongwa tries to reclaim the ball and Man City get back in possession.

It’s actually three Samba brothers at City. The youngest, Emerson, is also in the academy.

Early foul on Allan gets Man City a free kick and they have started as everyone expected they would – in plenty of possession.

They look for the early goal as O’Reilly feeds him in the from the left side, but the shot is blocked.

With just over 10 minutes until kick-off here are the teams for tonight’s fixture:

Man City XI: Rulli; O’Reilly, Vitor Reis, Khusanov, Lewis; Kovacic (c), Bouaddi; Ait-Nouri, Cherki, Allan; Samba

Subs: Anderson, Braithwaite, Donnarumma, Fernández, Guéhi, McAidoo, Ndiaye, Matheus Nunes, Semenyo

Norwich City XI: Grimshaw; Yongwa, Bruno Alves, Darling (c), Fisher; Field, Wright; Diallo, Ben Slimane, Crnac; Kvistgaarden

Subs: Chrisene, Mattsson, Kovacevic, Maghoma, McConville, Musaba, Schwartau, Stacey, Touré

"It's part of the decision that I took when I decided to join this club"Enzo Maresca responds to the doubts surrounding him filling Pep Guardiola's shoes 👇 pic.twitter.com/o6eUjQUOnU

David 🆚 Goliath 🤝🎥 https://t.co/5YXw2tQvfX pic.twitter.com/fTp9zD0xiX

As Abdukodir Khusanov makes his fourth start of the season, Hugo Viana, Man City director of football, has been speaking about the young Uzbek. The 22-year-old signed a new five-year contract with City in July, and Viana has affirmed that he “will be one of the best centre-backs in the world”.

"Abdukodir Khusanov will be one of the best centre-backs in the world" - Hugo Viana 🇺🇿🌏Full interview 🔗 https://t.co/dk3Qi8DF8D pic.twitter.com/hHdVdX5HSF

It’s nine changes for Norwich from the squad that lost 4-3 to Middlesbrough on the weekend.

Norwich goalkeeper Daniel Grimshaw came through the ranks at Manchester City, joining as a teenager, so this will be a special night for the 28-year-old.

Speaking of Phil Foden, the winger will not be making an appearance tonight, as he is serving his three-match suspension following his sending off in the Manchester derby. The England international lashed out at Bruno Fernandes after the United captain had fouled him, resulting in a red card for violent conduct.

As well as this fixture, he will also be missing City’s game against Sunderland and the trip to Anfield to face Liverpool the following weekend.

We broke down the incident as it happened on Sunday and you can get the full story here

Heavy squad rotation (10 changes in total for Maresca) has handed debuts for Gero Rulli in goal, as well as Allan and Floyd Samba in the outfield.

17-year-old Samba is the latest from City’s academy to be making his debut in the senior squad, following in the footsteps of Phil Foden, Rico Lewis, Nico O’Reilly and many more. A versatile midfielder, he has totalled 24 appearances across six competitions (incl Premier League 2) and scored 17 and assisted six goals in those matches.

Keep your eyes on young midfielder Floyd Samba, who has been handed his Manchester City debut tonight against Norwich by manager Enzo Maresca. Floyd is the 17 year old son of former Blackburn Rovers defender Christopher Samba.

His older brother Tyrone, 18, also plays for City. The siblings played in City’s FA Youth Cup final win over Manchester United last season, with Floyd scoring the first in a 2-1 win.

City fans will also be keen to see how Allan Elias gets on on his first start, having arrived from Palmeiras for £34m. Geronimo Rulli also debuts in goal.

#1653. GdS: Four exclusions, four defeats – Milan’s Pulisic dependance highlighted

There are many ways to outline Christian Pulisic’s importance to AC Milan, but one of them is very simple: wins.

La Gazzetta dello Sport have outlined the fact that when Pulisic starts a match, Milan do not lose. In an inconsistent team like Ruben Amorim’s, the four defeats this season to Benfica, Bournemouth, Bologna and Ferencvaros have two things in common.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The first is the two starters in midfield: four times out of four, the double pivot was Yunus Musah and Ardon Jashari each time. Then, there are the three absentees: Mario Gila, Luka Modric and Pulisic.

Pulisic, Gila and Modric are clearly three of Milan’s key players, and the American arguably more so than the others. He’s eighth in Serie A in points average from starts (2.67 points, five wins in six games).

Pio Esposito, Lulli, Mora (the three who have always won as starters), Zaccagni, Dimarco, Isaksen, and Zielinski rank higher, but there’s a clear difference: the others play for Lazio, Inter, and Roma, the top three in the league.

Captain America came on against Benfica, Bologna, and Ferencvaros, and was an unused substitute against Bournemouth. Compared to Modric, who has been playing consistently since August, and Gila, who has been affected by injury, Pulisic has had his ups and downs.

He scored in Udine, the derby and most recently against Genoa, and it’s no coincidence that the Diavolo won all three games. Simply put: when Christian plays well, Milan follow him. When his level drops, Milan struggle.

It’s tactics, as well as numbers. Pulisic has different characteristics from his team-mates: he’s the only one who attacks the space in behind. Gonçalo Ramos often comes deep and lays it off, Alphadjo Cisse loves having the ball at his feet, and CP disrupts defences in other ways.

Furthermore, he’s considered one of the owners’ key players, who are also American, and he just renewed his contract. If you have to imagine the Milan of the future, just think Pulisic and 10 others.

#1652. New Bromley boss Karl Robinson heaps praise on 'megastar' Jermain Defoe - with Premier League legend in talks over dugout return after walking out on Woking

Published: 08:00 EST, 6 November 2026 | Updated: 13:33 EST, 7 November 2026

New Bromley boss Karl Robinson has hailed Premier League 'megastar' Jermain Defoe as the ultimate professional following his abrupt departure from Woking.

Daily Mail Sport revealed on Tuesday that Defoe is in talks to join Robinson's backroom staff at League One strugglers Bromley after Andy Woodman's dismissal last month.

And while his appointment has yet to be confirmed, Robinson jumped at the chance to wax lyrical about Defoe at his inauguration on Thursday.

Bromley sit bottom of League One but their new boss believes Defoe's meticulous attention to detail would help the players find another gear.

'There's been a lot of talk but there always is with names like Jermain Defoe, who is a megastar. He's one of the greatest Premier League strikers of all time,' Robinson said.

'I have to raise and change the narrative of what this stands for,' the new boss pointed to the Bromley badge on his jumper.

Jermain Defoe is in talks to join League One strugglers Bromley as Karl Robinson's assistant

Former Salford City manager Robinson has hailed 'megastar' Defoe as the ultimate professional

'I have to bring people in to make me the best version of myself. I spoke to people who know Jermain and played with him.

'He was always first in. All the players who have played with him will tell you that. Steven Gerrard will tell you that.

'He was first in and still in the training ground at 4pm - massages, recovery, gym, video analysis of the players he's playing against.

'I was speaking to him about something completely different the other day and we were talking about discipline and professionalism.

'I said to him: "what do you do that for?". He went: "If I do everything right Monday to Friday and I play poorly, I can accept it because I've done everything in the week to be the best version of myself."

'I'm listening and I've got goose pimples on my arm. Then I'm thinking, that's probably why you're Jermain Defoe, because he did everything he possibly could to maximise his talent.

Defoe has been out of work since walking away from National League side Woking after just four months at the helm amid a strained relationship with the club's director of football.

The 44-year-old took charge of the final six games of last season and was expected to lead the club into the new campaign.

However, he failed to report for work on the eve of the season before contacting the club later that day to inform them he would not be returning.

The former England international and Tottenham Hotspur striker would add top-level experience to the dressing room, having scored 163 Premier League goals in 496 appearances - ranking 10th on the Premier League's scoring charts.

Robinson spoke as though he idolised Defoe when quizzed on his potential appointment, highlighting his humility and relentlessness as key assets to succeed as a coach.

'Failure isn't falling short, it's when you don't maximise your talent. And I think some of the players here haven't maximised their athletic, technical and tactical capabilities', Robinson added.

'For whatever reason, we need to find the key to what that is. I think someone like Jermain (would bring that) because he maximised everything he was and everything he is.

'That's almost the secret behind the genius of the top players. It's their attention to detail, professionalism and discipline – he does that over and over again.

'He's tried to manage in non-league as well. That, in itself, is dropping your ego to learn.'

Although Bromley are still working on finalising Defoe's appointment, he is expected to join Robinson in the dugout at Hayes Lane. The Ravens host Rotherham in the first round of the FA Cup this weekend as Robinson takes his first game in charge.

#1651. Michael Carrick: Man United's worst starts to a Premier League season and where the ex-England international ranks

By Joshua Cole | 12 Nov 2026 16:37

Manchester United have sacked Michael Carrick following their worst start to a Premier League season, with the former midfielder paying the price for a disastrous opening to the 2026-27 campaign.

The Red Devils were expected to build on last season's encouraging third-place finish after Carrick guided them back into the Champions League, but their performances have deteriorated dramatically since the summer.

Sunday's 4-4 draw against Aston Villa proved the final straw for the club's hierarchy, with United having collected just eight points from their opening 10 league matches to leave them 18th in the table.

Their solitary victory during that period represents a particularly concerning statistic for a club of their stature, especially considering that they had finished the previous campaign among the Premier League's top three.

Carrick's dismissal has therefore brought renewed attention to the club's historical struggles, with the 2026-27 campaign now ranking as their worst opening to a Premier League season after nine matches.

While United have endured difficult starts in previous campaigns, their current situation is particularly alarming given the resources available to the club and their expectations of competing for Champions League qualification.

Here, Sports Mole looks at Manchester United's five worst starts to a Premier League season, examining the results, circumstances and eventual outcomes of those campaigns.

Manchester United's current campaign sits at the bottom of this unwanted ranking, with Carrick's team collecting just seven points from their opening nine Premier League matches before the situation deteriorated further against Aston Villa.

Their only victory during that period came against Ipswich Town, while draws against Everton, Fulham, Tottenham and Leeds exposed their inability to turn promising situations into maximum points.

Defeats against Hull City, Manchester City, Bournemouth and Chelsea further increased the pressure on Carrick, whose team struggled to establish any consistency in their performances.

The 1-1 draw against 10-man Tottenham was particularly frustrating, while their inability to secure three points against Aston Villa despite scoring four goals demonstrated the defensive problems that had undermined their campaign.

United eventually reached 10 matches with eight points, leaving them 18th in the table and prompting the hierarchy to dismiss Carrick on November 12.

According to Opta Analyst, this is their worst start to a Premier League season, with the previous lowest return being 10 points after nine matches in 2019-20.

Ole Gunnar Solskjaer endured a difficult opening to his first full season as Manchester United manager, with the Norwegian struggling to build on the optimism generated during his initial caretaker spell.

United collected only 10 points from their first nine Premier League matches, winning two, drawing four and losing three, with their problems in front of goal becoming increasingly apparent.

Their campaign included disappointing draws against Wolverhampton Wanderers, Southampton and West Ham United, while a 2-0 defeat against West Ham at the London Stadium left Solskjaer facing growing criticism.

A 1-1 draw against Liverpool at Old Trafford on October 20 offered some encouragement, although United subsequently lost against Bournemouth before returning to winning ways against Norwich City.

Solskjaer ultimately survived the difficult opening and guided United to a third-place finish, collecting 66 points from 38 matches and securing Champions League qualification.

Erik ten Hag's third season at Old Trafford began disappointingly, with Manchester United collecting just 11 points from their opening nine Premier League fixtures.

The Red Devils won three, drew two and lost four of those matches, with their performances raising serious questions about Ten Hag's ability to deliver consistent improvement.

A 3-0 home defeat against Liverpool in September was particularly damaging, while subsequent losses against Tottenham and West Ham United increased the pressure on the Dutchman.

United also struggled to score consistently, with their attacking approach lacking the organisation and effectiveness required to compete with the leading sides.

The 2-1 defeat against West Ham on October 27 proved to be Ten Hag's final match, with the club dismissing him the following day.

He departed with United sitting 14th in the table, having collected just 11 points from nine matches, and was replaced by Sporting Lisbon manager Ruben Amorim.

David Moyes's successor, Louis van Gaal, also experienced a difficult introduction to life at Manchester United, with the Dutchman taking over following the club's disastrous seventh-place finish under the Scot.

Despite arriving with an impressive managerial reputation and having guided the Netherlands to the World Cup semi-finals in Brazil, Van Gaal struggled to establish consistency during his first few months.

United won three, drew four and lost two of their opening nine Premier League matches, collecting 13 points as their defensive problems continued from the previous campaign.

A 5-3 defeat against Leicester City in September was particularly damaging, with United surrendering a two-goal advantage against the newly promoted Foxes.

However, Van Gaal gradually improved the team's performances, with victories against Crystal Palace, Arsenal and Liverpool helping them secure fourth place with 70 points.

Although his first season was far from convincing, he restored Champions League football before eventually being dismissed in May 2016, shortly after winning the FA Cup.

Ten Hag's second season at Manchester United also began with considerable difficulties, despite the Dutchman having guided the club to a third-place finish and Carabao Cup success during his first campaign.

United won five and lost four of their opening nine Premier League matches, collecting 15 points, with their performances suggesting that the progress made previously had begun to stall.

A 3-1 defeat against Arsenal was followed by losses against Brighton and Bayern Munich, while a 3-0 home defeat against Manchester City further exposed the gap between United and the Premier League's leading teams.

Although they subsequently recovered to finish eighth with 60 points, their lowest Premier League position at the time, Ten Hag's future remained uncertain.

He was eventually dismissed in October 2024 following another disappointing opening to the following campaign, with the club deciding that a change was necessary after failing to see sufficient progress.

#1649. Next Man Utd manager: Mauricio Pochettino timeline 'revealed' with two-game delay possible

By Carter White | 12 Nov 2026 16:40

Manchester United have reportedly agreed to wait until next week to have Mauricio Pochettino at their Carrington training base.

The Red Devils are on the hunt for a new first-team head coach following the dismissal of Michael Carrick on Thursday morning, with the 20-time English champions sitting 18th in the Premier League standings.

Man Utd have managed to win just one of their opening 10 top-flight contests, with that sole success coming at Old Trafford against newly-promoted Ipswich Town at the end of the summer.

With the managerial position now vacant at the Theatre of Dreams, USA coach Pochettino has emerged as the favourite to take the reins, with the Argentine heading towards a return to the Premier League.

The 54-year-old has managed both Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea in the past, taking the former London club to the Champions League final in 2019, when they lost to Jurgen Klopp's Liverpool.

The process of appointing Pochettino is not straightforward, with the Argentine currently in position as the head coach of the United States, who have a two-legged quarter-final with Haiti in the CONCACAF Nations League over the next week.

As per ESPN, Manchester United are confident of agreeing personal terms with their top managerial target before the close of play on Thursday (November 12), after which point they will trigger the release clause in the coach's contract.

The report claims that the Red Devils will need to fork out £7m to take Pochettino away from the Stars and Stripes, with the 54-year-old's representatives supposedly contacting the Premier League giants to make them aware of the clause.

Surprisingly, Man Utd are said to be relaxed about the former Spurs boss staying in post with the United States for their double-header against Haiti, with the second leg taking place late on Tuesday night.

As a result, Pochettino is likely to arrive at the Red Devils' Carrington training base on next Wednesday (November 18) - just a few days before a crunch Premier League clash at Liverpool on November 22.

There is seemingly a chance that Pochettino takes charge of the United States twice more before departing to Manchester United, who are in danger of a relegation dogfight this season.

Whilst the Red Devils will be keen to have the Argentine in England as quickly as possible, there is also a realisation that the majority of the club's senior stars are currently away on international duty.

By the time Pochettino arrives at Carrington next Wednesday, most of Man United's first team players will have finished their national matches, focused on turning around the fortunes of England's grandest club.

Over the years, he's had the pleasure of interviewing some of the biggest names in world sport, including Usain Bolt, Rafael Nadal, Christian Pulisic, and more.

Crystal Palace are reportedly considering their managerial options after a difficult start to the Premier League season, with former Nottingham Forest boss Sean Dyche emerging as a potential replacement for Pierre Sage.

The Eagles’ disappointing results have increased pressure on Sage, whose side suffered a 2-0 defeat to Newcastle United on Sunday.

With Palace struggling near the relegation zone, the club could face an important decision over whether to persist with their current manager.

According to The Telegraph, Dyche is among the leading candidates should Palace decide to part ways with Sage.

#1644. Man Utd legend brands Sir Jim Ratcliffe, Omar Berrada conduct 'disgusting' following classless Michael Carrick dismissal

By Carter White | 12 Nov 2026 17:13

Manchester United legend Gary Neville has criticised the club's treatment of outgoing head coach Michael Carrick.

With the Red Devils sitting 18th in the Premier League table, the decision has been made to part ways with their former midfielder, who took charge of first-team matters from Ruben Amorim in January.

United States head coach Mauricio Pochettino is the clear favourite to take the reins at Old Trafford, with Man Utd supposedly reaching an agreement in principle for the former Tottenham Hotspur boss.

That being said, it is understood that the 54-year-old could still be in the dugout for the Stars and Stripes as they face Haiti in the quarter-finals of the CONCACAF Nations League over the next few days.

The highlight of Pochettino's career in England was undoubtedly taking Spurs to the Champions League final in 2019, with the Lilywhites eventually losing to Mohamed Salah, Jurgen Klopp and Liverpool.

Speaking to Sky Sports News, ex-Manchester United defender Neville has branded the club's treatment of Carrick as "disgusting", insisting that the Red Devils have gone about their latest managerial dismissal in the wrong way.

"In the last 24-48 hours it has been spectacularly bad to be in Monaco as an executive (Omar Berrada) and an owner (Sir Jim Ratcliffe) whilst your manager, who is a club legend, is taking training on the pitch and simultaneously approaching the US Soccer Federation to approach  Pochettino," said Neville.

"It is just quite simply disgusting. That falls well below the standard of what you would expect in any other business, in any other industry. It would be constructive dismissal and you would be getting sued.

"The optics of being in Monaco whilst the team, the staff, the people who are running the club on a day-to-day basis are in Manchester, it is just not good and it reflects badly on the leadership. I do not think anybody comes out of this well at all."

Carrick was relieved of his Man Utd duties after winning just three of 15 competitive matches at the beginning of the 2026-27 season, with the club in danger of experiencing a relegation battle this term.

As alluded to by Neville, Manchester United CEO Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox visited co-owner Ratcliffe in Monaco on Wednesday (November 11) to discuss the future of Carrick.

Wilcox and Berrada both advised the Red Devils' owner that the best course of action would be to dismiss the legendary midfielder after the club's worst start to a Premier League season in 40 years.

Whilst these meetings were taking place in Monte Carlo, Carrick remained at base and in position on the Carrington training pitches, coaching the first-teamers who are not involved on the international scene over the next week.

#1643. Osmand proves he's no Honda Civic... and now he's ready to motor on for Celtic

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 13:00 EST, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 13:48 EST, 7 November 2026

When Brendan Rodgers returns to Glasgow for a Q&A session next June, it would feel like a waste of time for him to be grilled on the exact reasons behind his team selection for matches which, by then, will have taken place almost two years ago.

Frankly, those assembled in the Royal Concert Hall that evening will have their mind on other matters.

Nonetheless, there remains a curiosity about why the Northern Irishman overlooked Callum Osmand at a time when Celtic were evidently crying out for a spark up front.

Rodgers, you may well remember, had spoken with great excitement about the club signing the player from Fulham a few weeks previously.

Sure, Osmand was only 19 at the time. He hadn't played a single minute of first-team football, either.

But as a combination of Daizen Maeda and the soon-to-depart Adam Idah failed to find the net across 210 minutes against Kairat Almaty, you couldn't help but wonder if the much-vaunted teenager stationed on the bench in both legs might have been worth a shot.

Despite Rodgers giving Osmand the big build up that summer, the forward didn't play a single minute prior to his abrupt departure at the end of October.

While that was clearly his prerogative, the impact Osmand has made across an injury-stricken year does suggest that it was an oversight.

Handed his debut as a substitute by Martin O'Neill against Falkirk soon after, Osmand scored a brilliant flashing header in the League Cup semi-final against Rangers before sustaining a serious hamstring tear against Midtjylland.

Only back in contention on the final day of the season after surgery, he set up Maeda and scored himself as Celtic clinched the title in dramatic fashion against Hearts.

Having been sidelined again with an ankle injury at the outset of this campaign, he's rebounded in some style. His goal and assist for Camilo Duran against Besiktas on Thursday came a couple of weeks after scoring twice in a 7-1 rout against the Tynecastle men in what was his first senior start.

Callum Osmand made an instant impression off the bench against Besiktas

After just 13 matches for Celtic, it may be a little too early to describe Osmand as a Ferrari. But a Honda Civic, he is most certainly not.

The beauty of the situation, from the club's perspective, is that the player hasn't even revved the engine as he sets out on his career path.

Osmand, who turns 21 as Kilmarnock visit today, looks first-team ready any time he's taken the field. Yet he's the first to admit that the game-time those injuries denied him stunted his development.

Provided there's a fair wind at his back, though, he's certain there's a lot more to come.

'I would say I'm nowhere near where I want to be personally,' he said.

'There's stuff I need to tidy up on, like decision-making and all this stuff.

'But I feel like the more games I play, the more I understand and the more I learn.

'So, on a personal note, that's what I'd want to do - just keep learning and keep understanding my role within the team and obviously the players you're playing with.

'I've still only played a handful of games, so it's tough learning. But I feel like when you get thrown in the deep end, it's the best way to learn. You learn more off the worst games than the good games.

'It's just as long as I can get better every game, that's all I really want to focus on.'

There's no doubt, though, that there are many moments when he looks the real deal.

For instance, his brilliant finish after Callum McGregor's square ball on Thursday, his first touch after coming off the bench.

'It was crazy,' he smiled. 'It's a surreal feeling when it's my first touch as well.

'I was a bit nervous that I'd shanked it, but no, I'm happy that I caught it nicely.'

One of his next involvements wasn't too bad, either. Motoring into space off the left flank, Osmand had to find the perfect weight and direction on the pass which would allow Camilo Duran to exploit a pocket of space and round the keeper. He could not have played it better.

Osmand has struck up a good understanding with fellow Celtic striker Camilo Duran

'I thought he was offside, to be honest,' he recalled of the moment in which Celtic moved 2-1 in front.

'I was looking at the bench saying 'Close?' and they were like, "Yeah, it's tight".

'But I know where he's going. He's such a sharp striker, so I know if I put that in the space, the keeper is not getting anywhere near it. He's a top, top player, so I can't fault him at all.'

With all due respect to Colby Donovan – also assured after coming off the bench – Thursday night will long be remembered for the belated contributions of Osmand and Duran, who scored three goals between them.

The Colombian began on the right flank, but moved infield once Kasper Hogh tired. The understanding Duran had with Osmand was clear throughout and ultimately proved the undoing of the Turks.

'He's unbelievable, a really top player,' Osmand said. 'You can just see even by the way he walks and the way he moves.

'I learn off him every day. He's an amazing guy. His English is really not great, but somehow we manage to talk to each other a lot.

'I think I find him quite a good friend of mine now.

'And although we might not speak many words, you can tell just by looking ... I don't know how to describe it. Like we talk to each other a lot. Maybe it's little words, but I feel like we get on really well. He's a great guy.'

Duran's finish at the second attempt to seal the victory later on felt hugely significant for all associated with Celtic.

It was precisely the kind of big win at the right moment which O'Neill and his embattled squad needed to blow away the storm clouds. On such moments, entire seasons can hinge and reputations are forged.

'For us, it felt like a must win, like that was our sort of mindset going into that,' Osmand said.

'I think the boys did amazing, so hopefully we just get some confidence and build on from this and that gives us confidence to play more free and take more risks.

'Sometimes when you're not as confident, it's tough to play the football you want to play.'

#1641. Thomas Tuchel faces fight to win trust of England players

Thomas Tuchel faces a fight to regain the full trust of his England players, despite claiming that “99.9 per cent” of supporters do not talk about the semi-final defeat by Argentina.

Telegraph Sport reported that players were shocked and disappointed by Tuchel’s approach to the final 30 minutes of the World Cup semi-final.

It can now be revealed that doubts linger among England players over Tuchel’s ability to get the best out of his squad and ultimately lead them to glory in the next European Championship.

There is also some lasting unhappiness over Tuchel’s perceived unwillingness to take ultimate responsibility for England’s World Cup exit and his claim that ball possession was not in “the DNA” of the nation’s players.

Tuchel has spoken of fostering a “brotherhood” within the England squad, but a source told Telegraph Sport: “He still has work to do to get all the players fully behind him again. What happened at the World Cup and some of his comments caused some damage that has not just disappeared.”

Tuchel has no concerns over the commitment of his players and said: “I have no doubt how keen they are. No doubt. I know them, I was seven weeks with them. We had a qualification campaign together, we are 18 months together, I have no doubt that we step up and produce performances in the next cycle. I’m responsible for that.”

One player who did not travel to the World Cup and is not part of Tuchel’s latest England squad for four Nations League games is Morgan Gibbs-White. His partner, Britney De Villiers, took a swipe at Tuchel by posting an image on Instagram that referenced the fact the Nottingham Forest man is the only Premier League player to have created five or more chances in every match he has played this season.

There is no immediate sign that Tuchel is ready to change his approach, as he refused to accept the country were angered by his tactics and substitutions in the Argentina game.

In an attempt to gloss over the nature of England’s missed opportunity in the United States, Tuchel claimed that the bronze-medal victory over France was “one of the nicest experiences ever” for supporters and that he did not lose any sleep over his World Cup squad selection.

Tuchel’s defence of the World Cup campaign also included the revelation that his Football Association bosses had assured the England head coach that his job was safe before the last-16 victory over Mexico.

“I tell you something, like 99.9 per cent of the fans don’t speak about substitutions, tactical twists,” Tuchel said. “They speak about where they have watched the Mexico game, they speak about the second half, the energy of the Croatia match, they speak about how nerve-wracking it was to watch our match against Congo and where they celebrated.

“This is how it should be, this is what a World Cup is for, to connect with the people and to give them experiences that they will not forget. And this is the feedback that I get.”

Asked if he had received any negative feedback at all since the World Cup, Tuchel answered: “No. Not at all. Do you think that’s necessary? I had some quite bad stuff between Argentina and France. [But] No [not since I’ve been back in England].”

The FA publicly backed Tuchel after the defeat by Argentina, but the German has now revealed that he was privately told his job was safe well before that.

Even if England had lost to Mexico and failed to reach the last eight of the World Cup, Tuchel has claimed he would not have been sacked. He said: “There was a moment, a very special moment, before the Mexico game where we had a talk and my bosses told me ‘we know that anything can happen in a football match, we know that anything can happen in a match in Mexico, in a World Cup match, but don’t worry, we see what’s going on and we want to continue like this’.

“It was a beautiful moment for me as a coach. I felt this kind of freedom to take my choices and to just coach freely, and there was never a doubt in my mind that we would continue together and there was obviously never a doubt in their mind.”

England secured their best World Cup finish since 1966 by winning the bronze-medal game against France in a chaotic match in Miami.

“If you look at the 6-4 against France, people talk about it like it’s one of their nicest experiences ever, to watch a football match,” Tuchel said. “So maybe I have to compromise in my wish for control, for a little bit more chaos, embrace the chaos, and maybe it brings out the best.”

Tuchel has named his first England squad since the World Cup for four Nations League games against Spain, Czech Republic (home and away) and Croatia. He has recalled Cole Palmer and Trent Alexander-Arnold to his squad, but insists he has lost no sleep over not taking the pair to the World Cup.

“I was very happy with the [World Cup] squad selection, we put a lot of effort and emphasis into the squad selection,” Tuchel said. “And I had a lot of sleepless nights, but I had not one sleepless night about our selection, because I was more than seven weeks with this group of players, and they were nothing but fantastic. I think the spirit that we built and the mentality that we showed brought us to the place that we got.

“It feels unfulfilled, but, yeah, that’s how it is. We need to move forward with the decisions in the Argentina game. And sometimes as a coach, you can only win if you win. So now we know the result, and we didn’t win. Of course, I reflect and, of course, I’m very critical of myself. But the question that is also still lingering around is, who knows what would have happened? Who knows if we hadn’t made any substitutions what would have happened? And would we have the same sleepless nights?

“So, there’s not much sense in torturing ourselves, looking back. It’s moving forward, but the team, like I said, did brilliantly. And I will not allow 30 minutes against Argentina to override how we view this World Cup.”

Tuchel had warnings for Palmer and Alexander-Arnold, as he said: “It is one thing to be nominated, by the way, with Cole and getting your ticket back in the squad, but it’s another thing to play and keep your place. It’s about when he comes and he needs to show these kinds of performances.”

On Alexander-Arnold, Tuchel added: “Now it’s time to fight for his place. He always said he’s up for a fight, especially for England. So it’s a need to prove that.”

Tuchel said that Alexander-Arnold has been called up as a right-back, rather than a midfielder. Asked if the Real Madrid player offers enough defensively, he answered by saying: “He has to, he has to. It’s necessary. My conviction is that he will, but he has no choice.”

Tuchel has now finished his broadcast duties. It was quite a strange performance from him. I don’t recall ever seeing him read from notes before. His little joke about his bosses telling him off was awkward and felt rehearsed, and the stuff about 99.9 per cent of England fans talking about Mexico and the second half against Croatia was delusional.

It was also jarring to hear him claim that the FA had basically assured Tuchel that his job was safe straight after England beat Mexico. It was a special night, undoubtedly, but did it really deserve that sort of reaction?

“I wanted to give Jarrad a chance. It was a 51 per cent decision on Jarrad.

“I don’t have a clear picture on what he is all about and have a very clear picture on what Levi can bring us.”

“It makes no sense to nominate three, four, five number 10s. It just does not help anyone. We can see the form that Morgan [Gibbs-White] is in.

“It’s one thing to be nominated, but it’s another thing to perform. This also counts, especially Cole needs to step up to justify the nomination.”

“The minimum I can do is back my bosses. They have my full support on that.

“I’m grateful that I can talk about football because that’s my little bit of knowledge, not sports politics.”

“That’s the beauty of high-level sport, you can’t always win and it makes you feel alive. Not in a very nice way, still you feel that pain of these high-pressure moments.

“As soon as you enter knockout football, it’s a new level of pressure.”

Tuchel has now claimed that people say the 6-4 against France is “maybe one of their best experiences (watching football) ever”.

Again, not something anyone has said to me. Where is Tuchel finding these people?!

Tuchel on Alexander-Arnold: “He comes as a right back.” Sounds like he agrees with Mourinho that the Real Madrid player is not a midfielder.

Tuchel: “There was never a doubt in my mind that we would continue together and there was obviously never a doubt in their (the FA’s) mind.”

Tuchel says that 99.9 per cent of fans don’t talk about substitutions. He says they speak about the Mexico game and the Croatia game, their emotions and where they watched the matches.

He’s expecting Palmer to step up and show him his Chelsea form.

“When you are a coach, you only win when you win...There’s not much sense torturing ourselves by looking back. I will not allow 30 minutes of the World Cup to determine how we view the World Cup.”

Tuchel says he has no regrets over not taking Palmer and Alexander-Arnold to the World Cup. He says he didn’t have a single sleepless night over his squad selection.

Tuchel says the direction in sports is always forwards and never backwards. “The target is to win the home Euros, of course.”

Tuchel says his feelings on the World Cup are mixed. He thinks there are very positive things to take from the World Cup, but says it was also unfulfilled. He says it’s important to recognise that England won a bronze medal, but says he acknowledges they did not push it over the line.

He says the downside of having the belief they could go and win it is that it hurts even more that they did not.

Tuchel has said the France third-place game “directs the narrative” of what’s coming for England.

Tuchel will be happy with this so far. Very gentle start from the broadcasters.

No questions from the broadcasters about blowing the lead against Argentina and Tuchel’s opinion about the World Cup. Weird.

Ben White pulled out with an injury after being back to his best. It is unfortunately, a bit of a story for him. Josh King was very close and is on the radar.

Tuchel seems to be referring to notes as he speaks. He keeps looking down at a piece of paper he brought in with him.

“The door is always open through performance, behaviour and commitment.”

“They had a good start to the season. Now it’s a new competition. Some positions have injuries. Palmer has his numbers back and a point to prove. Trent was never non-selectable and comes in as a right back.”

We will be hearing from Tuchel very soon. Lots to discuss but the Palmer and Alexander-Arnold call-ups and his World Cup reflections are at the top of the list.

5 - Alex Scott is the only midfielder in the Premier League this season to rank in the top five for times he has won possession (3rd), for the number of duels contested (=4th) and for total distance covered (5th).Sprightly. pic.twitter.com/xfVzme7JXj

Jason Steele’s inclusion is effectively a call-up. He was at the World Cup as a “fourth” goalkeeper for training – and going to country and western gigs in Kansas – but was not part of the official 26-man squad.

The big ‘loser’ from the World Cup squad in being left out by Thomas Tuchel is Arsenal’s Noni Madueke. It is understood the place of his club team-mate Eberechi Eze was also in question, but the 28-year-old has been included, partly because of the unavailability of other players. Hopefully Thomas Tuchel will explain all later.

The absence of Nottingham Forest’s Morgan Gibbs-White is puzzling.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin is the top-scoring Englishman in the Premier League since the start of last season.

🎯 "CALVERT-LEWIN STICKS IT IN!" pic.twitter.com/UJ54wPGytV

Thomas Tuchel has named his England squad for the first games of the 2026-27 season, as the Three Lions begin a new Uefa Nations League campaign.

There’s a return to the Three Lions squad for a number of players following the start of the new campaign with their clubs, with the likes of Cole Palmer, Dominic Calvert-Lewin, Lewis Hall, Rio Ngumoha, Jarrad Branthwaite, Myles Lewis-Skelly and Alex Scott all selected.

And there’s a place in the squad for Trent Alexander-Arnold, alongside his Real Madrid teammate Jude Bellingham.
