#1516. Predicting how the USA would line up under Guardiola if dream appointment succeeds

Has anyone considered how the USA feel in all of this? They’re about to lose one of the most high-profile managers in the history of their men’s soccer team.

Manchester United are hurtling towards the appointment of Mauricio Pochettino at long last. He’s been on their radar for ages and now looks set to get the job.

But United’s gain will be the USMNT’s loss. Pochettino was a big appointment in 2024 in terms of global pedigree after the sacking of Gregg Berhalter and now US Soccer chiefs will have to find a suitable successor.

And according to reports, they’re dreaming big again. Even bigger this time, in fact. They’ve been talking about Pep Guardiola and, according to The Athletic, are likely to place him near the top of their wish list – probably after realising he’s pretty damn good.

It’d be ambitious. Guardiola walked away from management in the summer when he brought an end to his decade in charge of Manchester City. After all he achieved there, and at Barcelona and Bayern Munich before, he’s a GOAT contender when it comes to managers.

He’s earned a break from the touchline, but we wonder if the lower intensity of an international job might just reel him back in.

In the unlikely event the USA were to succeed in appointing him, here’s how we reckon he could set them up.

Guardiola has actually worked with an American goalkeeper before with Man City, but Zack Steffen has only played once for his country in the past four years.

Matt Freese is currently number one for the USA, but the New York City keeper isn’t the most convincing with the ball at his feet.

That’s usually a problem for Guardiola, who wasn’t afraid to bin off a long-serving starter in Joe Hart at the Etihad when he took charge over similar concerns.

He later regretted his treatment of Hart, so might not be so hasty in future, but there are other options waiting to take over in the American setup.

Kochen, currently on loan at Lyngby from Barcelona, is someone who might intrigue him. The 20-year-old has a better ball-playing reputation and will be looking to establish himself as the long-term number one for his country.

No need for a change at right-back. Dest is a pretty easy pick, nearly 50 caps into his international career.

At 26, the PSV and former Barcelona man should be sticking around for the long run.

Richards is someone Guardiola will be familiar with after coming up against him in the Premier League after the defender’s move to Crystal Palace in 2022.

Offering strength and an ability to bring the ball out from the back, he would be a good fit. And he’s already become one of the leaders in the national team anyway.

An even better ball player, McKenzie has a pass success rate of more than 90% in Ligue 1 with Toulouse this season.

At 27, he’s in the prime of his career and continues to thrive in one of Europe’s top leagues.

There were some reports in the tabloids around the start of the decade that Guardiola wanted to sign Fulham’s Robinson for City.

Whether it was true or not, who knows, but there’s no doubting the 29-year-old would still be a dependable option at left-back.

Guardiola would know all about what Robinson can offer from his time in the Premier League.

The current USA captain. Playing at a high level in the Premier League. He’s no Rodri or Xavi, but keeping Adams as a key figure makes sense.

Weston McKennie might be the bigger name, but Musah might be the better fit for a Guardiola team.

He’s improved for AC Milan this season and is well renowned for his press resistance, which is a crucial asset.

His versatility would also appeal to Guardiola, who likes players with the intelligence to cover multiple territories.

Weah largely plays at right-back at club level these days for Marseille, but still plays in the attack for the USA.

Like Musah, his ability to play in various roles would be a big tick for Guardiola. It’s on the right wing he’d probably be best stationed, at least until future Man City prospect Cavan Sullivan is ready for a bigger role.

In the number 10 role, Tillman could be the go-to man. He’s got good control and press resistance, making him a good fit.

Currently playing for Bayer Leverkusen, he has good pedigree after spells with PSV, Rangers and Bayern Munich.

The first place to look for star quality in the USA squad. He was only so-so in the Premier League with Chelsea, but you can’t argue with Pulisic’s record for his country.

He’s been in good form for AC Milan and isn’t going anywhere anytime soon in terms of the international picture.

No Erling Haaland to help Guardiola here. Not even a Sergio Aguero. But there are some decent American strikers he’d be able to pick from.

It’d likely be a battle between Pepi and Folarin Balogun for starting duties up front. Pepi might have the edge thanks to being slightly better at link-up play.

The PSV striker also knows how to thrive in tight spaces in the box and at 23 years old has plenty more goals in his destiny.

#1515. Bayern Munich: the news is increasingly worrying for Jamal Musiala

Clearly, you almost have to have a medical degree to follow Bayern Munich this season… The Bavarian giant is thus facing a fairly complicated start to the season in terms of injuries and health problems, starting with its coach, Vincent Kompany, hospitalized and currently on rest following a fairly significant burn-out. Several players on the squad are also at a standstill. Hit in the foot against Mainz, Manuel Neuer, the latest, will be on the sidelines for at least two months.

Ismael Saibari will also be absent for several months, while Luis Diaz and Serge Gnabry still have a few weeks of absence ahead of them due to muscle problems. We can therefore almost speak of a decimated workforce… Then comes the Jamal Musiala case. Appearing only 4 times this season, for just over 200 minutes played in total, the 23-year-old attacking midfielder is causing great concern across the Rhine.

This summer, following several illnesses, he explained that he was suffering from a neurological dysfunction, forcing him to undergo treatment and causing long periods of absence. Since then, he has hardly played, and even if he returned to collective training earlier this week, the latest revelations made by Uli Hoeness – honorary president of the club – are anything but reassuring. “He is in a complicated situation. He has an illness that is not easily treated. He can control it to a certain extent with medication. But we don’t know if he can perform like before.”indicated the leader on the radio Bayerischer Rundfunk.

“He is still receiving his salary, but now imagine if Bayern questioned his contract saying: ‘the current performance level is not that of his contract’”concluded Hoeness, who therefore suggested that for the moment, Bayern was not going to question the deal signed by the player in February 2025, and which places him among the highest salaries in the squad with 25 million euros received per season. A difficult case to manage, for the player obviously, but also for the staff and management of the club…

#1514. Russell must do something wacky now after disappointing Bahrain GP qualifying

Never mind the lack of an ice vest, George Russell is somehow going to need to be the coolest man in Malaysia if he is to turn seventh on the grid into a positive result in Sunday’s Bahrain Grand Prix.The first race in Sepang in nearly a decade – a late addition to the calendar because of the conflict in the Middle East – promises to be an absolute scorcher. It might even be worth setting your alarm for the 8am UK start time. Red Bull’s Max Verstappen will start in pole position for the first time this year. He will have Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton alongside him.

It will be the first time since Hungary 2023 that those two gladiators have started on a front row together. Throw in sweltering temperatures, low grip, high tyre degradation, and the ever-present threat of a Malaysian monsoon sweeping through Sepang, and you have the potential for fireworks.

Russell might need something wacky if he is to do anything from that far back. This was a desperately disappointing result for the British driver. After his victory in Baku last weekend, Russell was hopeful he had finally found the winning formula and that he could continue to take the fight to his team-mate Kimi Antonelli, whom he trails in the drivers’ championship by 66pts.

Eighth, four places behind, and 0.24sec slower than the Italian, was not what Russell would have had in mind, although both Mercedes drivers will rise a spot because of the five-place grid penalty meted out to Red Bull’s Isack Hadjar for exceeding his engine allowance for the season.Russell will have felt particularly disappointed as Antonelli only got one run in Q3 after using up a set of soft tyres when he made a mistake and went off track in Q2. He now trails his team mate nine-seven in qualifying head-to-head this year.“No to be honest,” Russell admitted when asked whether he knew why he was so slow. “This circuit is an outlier in terms of the abrasiveness of the tarmac.“The lap times seven years ago were six or seven seconds faster and at certain points on the track it feels like you are driving on gravel, which is the same for everyone, but it is clearly affecting us more than others.”Mercedes’ lack of performance was doubly unexpected because not only did they arrive here with a massive upgrade package, but Russell revealed this week that he and Antonelli were foregoing the cooling vests you see some drivers sporting on the grid, in favour of car performance.

Toto Wolff, the Mercedes team principal, admitted it was a head-scratcher. “Very difficult to understand,” the Austrian said. “We have been a little bit caught out on Friday with some car behaviour that we did not see all year, but then you can say it is very hot and the tarmac is different to all the [other] tracks. It looked really good this morning. We seemed to have, at least with Kimi, made a step in understanding. And then, qualifying was a little bit back to what we saw before, just no performance.”

Still, both titles are in the bag so Wolff cannot be too unhappy. Russell is the one who will be really miffed. He really needs to be beating his team-mate pretty much every race weekend if he is to get his title hopes back on track.

At the front, the mood was somewhat different. Verstappen became the first non-Mercedes-powered pilot to take a pole position this year. It was a first pole position for Red Bull Powertrains, too. And with his long run pace looking more than decent, Verstappen should really hold on for his first win of 2026. Hamilton will do his best to hang on to the Dutchman’s coattails. The seven-time champion was delighted when told he had taken P2. “Let’s go guys! Finally! Great job guys, really great job. Car felt great.”

This was indeed an excellent performance from the Ferrari man – and just the tonic for the Scuderia after weeks of gossip and speculation. Hamilton was admittedly three tenths slower than his rival, which he put purely down to a power deficit on the straights, but he said he was hopeful his long run pace was more competitive. The last time a F1 held a race was held here back in 2017, the British driver claimed pole only to be overhauled by a youthful Verstappen. He will be desperate to turn the tables this time.

“It was really hard to find a good balance, and we made one change before qualifying and we hit the sweet spot,” he reflected afterwards. “I am so, so grateful. I will try my best to hold on to Max tomorrow, and if we are in the fight that would be awesome. I’ve been talking too much, but I guess you talk more when you are happy. It was my best lap of the year. It feels like I won, and I will give it everything tomorrow.”

It is Russell, though, who needs a result even more badly if he is to remain a factor in the championship. “As a team, we have yet to have a bad race this whole season and this was clearly a very bad qualifying for us,” he admitted, adding that “all the numbers” from the upgrade package suggested it was an improvement on the old car. “But I think there is going to be a lot happening tomorrow. The tyre deg is huge and race pace will be king. So even though today was a real disappointment it is not the be all and end all.”

No. 1 ☝️#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/01PqrckQS9

Tomorrow’s race will be the first time since Hungary 2023 that Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton will start on the front row together. It is a reasonable run down to turn one and there are overtaking opportunities through the first few corners at Sepang, with it being similar to the configuration in China, with plenty of lines and moves on offer.

Respect between two great champions 🤩#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/fbZ6aoKRyw

“Very difficult to understand. We have been a little bit caught out on Friday with some car behaviour that we did not see all year, but then you can say it is very hot and the tarmac is the different to all the (other) tracks. It looked really good this morning. We seemed to have, at least with Kimi [Antonelli], made a step in understanding. And then, qualifying was a little bit back to what we saw before, just no performance.”

On Kimi Antonelli’s track limits breach in Q2:

“Not good, because Q2 you know you are going to get through. You lose a set [of softs] in a qualifying that is so tight, where we are on the back foot. That is not good.”

Lewis Hamilton says this is the biggest crowd he has ever seen at Sepang, thanking the fans for making it here today. That is actually a bigger compliment than many watching at home may realise. The traffic this weekend has been horrendous. After 10 years without a race in Malaysia, during which time F1 has grown massively, I think they have forgotten how to do traffic management. Shuttles are inconsistent, taxis can’t get in/out, it’s taking forever just to reach the airport a few kilometres away - some fans have been braving the heat and walking. It took over two hours to get back into Kuala Lumpur last night (48km). My understanding is the Bahrainis are organising the race this year, while local forces are handling the traffic outside the circuit.

“The car has been very good since last week. It is good to come back [from his wrist injury] at such a time and I am enjoying it, fighting for the top three. Even though it was not my finest qualifying session it is a good feeling.

“It is a bit unfortunate we take a penalty on a track where we are that fast but, from eighth, I am confident we can come through the field and come back for a good result.”

“I love this energy [from the crowd]. Big, big thank you to Malaysia for welcoming us. It is so hot here. I keep saying it, but that has made it a massive challenge for the tyres, the car, the mechanics in the garage. I am really, really thankful to my team. We made so many changes through all these practice sessions. Because the cars are sliding, the tyres are overheating, it was really hard to find a good balance, and we made one last change going into qualifying and I think we hit the sweet spot. To be able to close the gap to two or three tenths to Max [Verstappen], who has been so quick all weekend, is great, and I am so grateful.

“I am much happier with where the car is, but tomorrow is a completely different ballgame. Making these tyres last around this track, they are overheating from the get-go. Every little bit of wheelspin you have, every little snap you have makes a difference of how far you are going to go. I like to think we have got a good balance. Max was really quick on his long runs, so I will just try my best to hold onto him tomorrow.”

A reminder that Isack Hadjar will drop from third to eighth after his grid penalty.

QUALIFYING CLASSIFICATIONCan't wait for Sunday! 🤩#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/qqi8hPDcKA

“It is fantastic. We have been trying many grand prix to get pole. Sometimes a bit closer than others but to finally get it, from where we started the season, pretty incredible. I am happy with today and, for sure, I am going to try and win tomorrow. When you start first, that is the target.”

Big disappointment that for Russell. After his win in Baku, where he said he finally felt hooked up to the car, he was desperate to build the momentum. P8, four places behind Antonelli, was not what he would have had in mind. Has it all to do in the race tomorrow.

Excellent (though not unexpected) pole for Verstappen, and a very good P2 for Hamilton. Could be some fireworks on the front row tomorrow.

*Hadjar’s three-place grid penalty will drop him down to eighth place for the race tomorrow.

Neither of the Red Bulls can improve in the first sector but it is those behind them who need significant improvements. The two Ferraris are going along nicely at the start of their final flying laps. Hadjar is unable to improve despite a purple final sector. Verstappen then goes fastest in the final sector and improves his advantage at the top.

Hamilton meanwhile went fastest in the middle sector and goes second fastest overall. Piastri cannot improve but stays ahead of Russell.

Norris is the final man across the line but is only fast enough for P6. That means that Verstappen takes pole in Malaysia, which is the first time this season that Red Bull have taken pole position. Hamilton is second with Hadjar third, although the Frenchman has a five-place grid penalty.

MAX VERSTAPPEN TAKES POLE FOR THE BAHRAIN GRAND PRIX IN MALAYSIA!! 👊#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/NgtaCAZacL

The two Red Bulls, who are one and two at the moment, will be the first two drivers across the line on these final efforts.

The other nine drivers in Q3 are in the pits so young Antonelli has the track to himself as he sets his one and only flying lap of Q3. He is over four tenths down on Verstappen through the first sector and has plenty of work to do.

The championship leader sets a decent middle sector where he loses no more time to Verstappen. As it stands he would put himself third before the others do their final runs. He comes across the line in P3 but will have the likes of Hamilton, Piastri, Leclerc, Norris and Russell trying to surpass him.

Russell is the first across the line and sets a time of a 1:36.032. He does not last long at the top as he is immediately displaced by Hadjar, who is half a second quicker.

Hamilton then comes over the line in second, just ahead of his teammate Leclerc. Piastri puts himself between the two Ferraris.

What about Verstappen? The man who won here the last time we were in Malaysia continues his great form today and goes quickest by more than three tenths.

Antonelli now heads out and will have the track to himself really. This is going to be the championship leader’s only flying lap of Q3.

Russell is the first man to head out for his first flying lap in Q3. Antonelli has remained in the pits with just one new set of softs remaining. Verstappen, who right now feels like the favourite for pole, will be one of the last across the line in these first attempts of Q3.

The fight for pole position in Sepang begins now as the green light is on at the end of the pit lane to get Q3 going.

Antonelli, due to that lap time deletion in Q2, has just one new set of softs for Q3, which could prove costly in his attempts to try and take pole.

P12 the best qualifying result of the season for Alonso. It was only his second time in Q2 after Hungary (P16).

I should add, P14 was also Lance Stroll’s best qualifying result of the season. His first outing in Q2 this year.

11. Liam Lawson (Racing Bulls)12. Fernando Alonso (Aston Martin)13. Carlos Sainz (Williams)14. Lance Stroll (Aston Martin)15. Franco Colapinto (Alpine)16. Arvid Lindblad (Racing Bulls)

With grid penalties already on their way, neither Colapinto nor Lindblad set lap times in Q2.

Verstappen, Leclerc, Piastri, Norris, Hadjar and Russell all remain in the pits. A bit of a risk for Russell down in eighth but his time should be enough to get into Q3.

Lindblad, who will start tomorrow’s race at the back of the grid after penalties, gives his teammate Lawson a tow down the back straight and it works as Lawson just sneaks into the top ten.

Can Bortoleto get back ahead though of Lawson? Yes he can and he will take the final place in Q3. Lawson thought he might be through but the tow was not enough.

Lindblad, who's taking a grid penalty for Sunday's race, gave team mate Lawson a tow but it wasn't quite enough to send the Kiwi into Q3#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/IMlrqg4ENv

As the young Italian starts his flying lap, there is no-one else out on track so no traffic. He is a lot more cautious at turn six this time than last time, when he had his lap time deleted.

He has not set blistering first and second sector times but a purple final sector puts him into second and the Italian is safely into Q3.

Plenty of other drivers are now heading around the track for their final flying laps of Q2.

11. Lance Stroll (Aston Martin)12. Carlos Sainz (Williams)13. Kimi Antonelli (Mercedes)14. Arvid Lindblad (Racing Bulls)15. Franco Colapinto (Alpine)16. Fernando Alonso (Aston Martin)

Mercedes have put a brand new set of softs onto Antonelli’s car as he heads out promptly, with no lap time to his name so far. Antonelli is still disputing the lap deletion over team radio but his team tell him the images show he exceeded track limits. This is now a lot of pressure on the championship leader; any mistake now and he will not make Q3. His teammate Russell is only in seventh.

Antonelli was fourth fastest but has had his lap time deleted for exceeding track limits at turn six. That is a big moment in Q2 and could prove problematic if he gets into Q3. Antonelli appeared to be confused when he was told about his lap deletion over team radio but the on-board view looked pretty clear-cut.

Piastri then comes across the line in third.

Here's the moment Kimi ran wide 👀#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/E0VdWdBt8x

The Dutchman looks in a great spot at the moment to take pole position today and his 1:35.696 is very quick. He is nearly four tenths quicker than Antonelli.

How about the Ferraris? Leclerc was quickest in the middle sector but is nearly three tenths down on Verstappen. Hamilton puts himself into third place. Russell is more than half a second down on Verstappen.

Verstappen has been shown a black and white flag for driving unnecessarily slowly. I doubt he will get a grid penalty for that but it will be a warning for the Dutchman.

Anyway, the drivers, other than Colapinto and Alonso, are on flying laps, with Verstappen currently fastest inthe first sector.

The green light is showing at the end of the pit lane and the second part of qualifying is under way. Like the start of Q1, it is hardly a stampede to go out.

17. Nico Hulkenberg (Audi)18. Oliver Bearman (Haas)19. Esteban Ocon (Haas)20. Alex Albon (Williams)21. Valtteri Bottas (Cadillac)22. Sergio Perez (Cadillac)

The Aston Martin of Stroll improves significantly from 20th and is set to make Q2, as is his teammate Alonso. A bit of a surprise to see the Aston Martins improve and make it into Q2.

Go Fernando! 🤩 Go Lance! 🤩First double Q2 appearance this season 🙌#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/xjiWYv6ycr

That has seen the Audi of Hulkenberg drop into the drop zone and the German is out. For contrast, his teammate improves to go into eighth place! Hulkenberg had a big lock up into turn 14, which proved very costly.

As it stands, eight of the top nine are remaining in the garage. Russell is in ninth and has not gone out but Gasly above him in eighth has. You would imagine Russell is perfectly safe.

17. Esteban Ocon (Haas)18. Alex Albon (Williams)19. Oliver Bearman (Haas)20. Lance Stroll (Aston Martin)21. Valtteri Bottas (Cadillac)22. Sergio Perez (Cadillac)

Ocon, in 17th, is quite far off Hulkenberg in 16th and needs more than four tenths to usurp him.

The screens in the media centre here in Sepang tell me that the air temp right now is 32.8C and the track temp is 58C. It feels even hotter. Lots of chat about cooling vests this week, which are optional. George Russell is among the drivers who isn’t using one, which is interesting a) because Russell has suffered badly from heat in the past (Qatar, Singapore) and b) because he says Mercedes chose to put the development money into car upgrades instead.

It’s an interesting admission. Not everyone is sold on the idea of cooling vests. Ferrari and McLaren will definitely be using them this weekend, for instance. Max Verstappen won’t as he doesn’t like them. Russell thinks the FIA should just develop the tech themselves and it shouldn’t be part of the budget cap.

“Our team have put a lot of emphasis this year on the cockpit temperature,” he said. “We won’t be running the cooling vest because we haven’t put the resource into making it robust enough. I feel we need the FIA just to step in and say ‘Here’s some money extra in the cost cap or there’s an external company who’s going to develop it for everybody’. Because we should all be wearing it. When it works, it works great. So, I would like to wear it this week, and I would like to wear it next week. But the team asked me...look, we can develop it, and we can put the money towards it...[but at a cost].

He added: “The top itself is not expensive ..you’ve got to effectively make a system where you can fit a block of dry ice or actual ice, and then has the airflow to circulate the cool water throughout. If that system isn’t robust enough, then suddenly you have no circulation, and then you get hot. You get ambient temperature circulating. The vest is one-design, but the system that circulates the water is different [at different teams].”

The two Ferraris are on medium tyres but Leclerc still puts himself into second place. He is then displaced by Hamilton, who slots in behind Verstappen. Good times from the Ferraris on the mediums.

What about the McLarens? Norris goes sixth fastest but is more than six tenths down on Verstappen. Then comes Piastri, who goes fourth fastest, just under four tenths off Verstappen.

Arguably the three favourites for pole; Antonelli, Russell and Verstappen, are all on flying laps.

The first sector goes the way of Verstappen, who is purple, and then the Dutchman goes purple in the middle sector.

Antonelli is two tenths faster than his teammate Russell but Verstappen is over half a second quicker than the Mercedes. Hadjar is then second fastest to show the pace in the Red Bull this weekend.

Most of the teams waited and waited to come out and then suddenly lots of drivers are sent out, resulting in a queue in the pits! With the high track temperatures and high degradation, the drivers are crawling around on their out laps to preserve these soft tyres.

Bumper to bumper in the pit lane! #F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/ff8JO9kB1g

The two Haas drivers have a free track to themselves whilst everyone else bides their time. In theory, as the hour of qualifying goes on, the track temperature should decrease and the more rubber that is laid down the faster the track should get.

Finally, just before the two Haas drivers finish their first flying laps, the rest of the grid is starting to emerge, led by the Mercedes duo.

The green light is showing at the end of the pit lane and Q1 is officially under way. The two Haas drivers are the first to head out. Other than that, it is a quiet start to Q1.

The top four teams; Mercedes, Red Bull, Ferrari and McLaren, all have a genuine chance of taking pole in Sepang today. I think the true favourites though have to be the Mercedes duo and Max Verstappen but with how close it between all four of the teams you cannot rule anything out.

It is 33 degrees celsius air temperature, with the track temperature up at 58 degrees.

Not long to wait now until qualifying begins. It is hot, humid and dry in Sepang right now. As we know in Malaysia, the weather can change quickly and thunderstorms can roll in quite quickly but it looks like today’s qualifying will be a dry one. This will be one of if not the hottest qualifying sessions of the season, so much so that we are seeing umbrellas going up to get some shade from the sun rather than sheltering from any rain.

This will be important to consider after qualifying finishes as there will be some shuffling around:

Isack Hadjar (Red Bull): five-place grid penalty- new internal combustion engineFranco Colapinto (Alpine): ten-place grid penalty- new engineFranco Colapinto (Alpine): five-place grid penalty- causing a collision in BakuArvid Lindblad (Racing Bulls): back of the grid- complete power unit change

Hadjar has looked good since returning from his wrist injury so could be fighting it out near the front of the grid, although his five-place penalty will drop him down. We know Lindblad will be at the back and is very likely to be joined there by Colapinto, who is not going to be qualifying high up in the top ten in his Alpine.

Haas have announced that Frenchman Esteban Ocon will leave at the end of this season. Ocon now faces an uncertain future, with it difficult to see a spot for him on the F1 grid next season. There are suggestions that the 30-year-old’s replacement will be Brazilian Ferrari junior Rafael Camara, although nothing has been confirmed on that front. 21-year-old Camara currently leads the Formula 2 championship.

TGR Haas F1 Team and Esteban Ocon will part ways at the conclusion of the 2026 season. With plenty of racing ahead, our focus remains on working together to maximize every opportunity through to the final race of the year.#HaasF1 #F1 pic.twitter.com/4iQAuqnSyA

Aston Martin have now confirmed their driver line-up for next season, retaining both Fernando Alonso and Lance Stroll. There had been reports that Alonso had been contemplating retirement but the 45-year-old will continue into another season.

Aston Martin Aramco confirms Lance and Fernando will continue as the team's drivers in 2027. Read more: ​https://t.co/ePyjJdyAIB pic.twitter.com/VogFUEbNxy

Other than the second seat alongside Ollie Bearman at Haas, the only other team to keep an eye on is Racing Bulls, with no definite confirmation on their exact driver line-up for next season.

Ferrari this week have publicly backed their team principal Frederic Vasseur, amid speculation over the Frenchman’s position and comments made by former Red Bull team principal Christian Horner, who said the job at Ferrari would be a “dream job”. Ferrari, who sit second in the constructors’ standings, have not won the drivers’ championship since 2007 (Kimi Raikkonen) and the constructors’ since 2008. Here is a snippet from Tom Cary’s piece on the matter:

In a hastily convened media call on Tuesday morning, Maria Conti, Ferrari’s chief communication officer, said the Scuderia had decided to issue a vote of confidence in Vasseur in response “not just to the story of Mr Horner, but in general, the speculation about Fred”.

“Ferrari has made its choices,” Conti said. “We have confidence – full confidence – in Fred Vasseur and in his team, and we continue to do so.

“At this time, it’s really important that the team remains united and cohesive, and we are focused with all the energy on the work ahead.”

“It is great to be back [in Malaysia]. I am really enjoying the track. We have had some wonderful races here over time. It is actually the 20th time we have been here, it started in 1999, and it is really exciting to be back. I really enjoyed getting out on the track and watching the cars closely.

“The drivers are super fit and they have some cooling but it is not easy. But you almost cannot get enough fluid through your body before your stomach gives up. Having this race and Singapore back-to-back increases that challenge.”

Especially with the big upgrade they have brought this weekend, Mercedes’ lead at the summit is looking unassailable right now.

Almost nine years ago to the day, Max Verstappen took just his second race victory in Formula 1. Lewis Hamilton, who took pole position, and Daniel Ricciardo joined Verstappen on the podium. Despite being nine years ago, plenty of drivers still on the grid were racing that weekend. Here they are and who they were racing for:

Max Verstappen (Red Bull) Lewis Hamilton (Mercedes) Valtteri Bottas (Mercedes) Esteban Ocon (Force India)Nico Hulkenberg (Renault)Sergio Perez (Force India)Fernando Alonso (McLaren)Lance Stroll (Williams)Carlos Sainz (Toro Rosso)Pierre Gasly (Toro Rosso)

With Russell winning in Baku and Antonelli finishing fifth, the latter’s championship lead was cut to 66 points. If Russell is going to usurp his teammate, he is going to need a few more similar results to last weekend due to the size of Antonelli’s lead. If Antonelli were to suffer a retirement, then that completely changes the outlook.

Formula One returns to Malaysia for round 16 of the season for the Bahrain Grand Prix. That probably sounds strange but after the Bahrain Grand Prix was originally postponed in March, F1 reinstated it to the calendar with Malaysia hosting it because of the ongoing war in the Middle East. Despite being held in Malaysia, Bahrain have retained the naming rights for the event, which is officially known as the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia. The last time Formula One was in Malaysia was nine years ago back in 2017, when a young whippersnapper named Max Verstappen, still four years away from winning his first world championship, claimed just his second victory.

Last time out around the streets of Baku, Mercedes’ George Russell claimed victory at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, pipping Verstappen by just a tenth of a second. That was Russell’s first grand prix win since June and cuts his team-mate Kimi Antonelli’s lead in the drivers’ standings to 66 points. Antonelli had a challenging weekend in Baku, starting 16th after a crash in qualifying and coming home in fifth to see his championship lead to Russell cut by 15 points.

Verstappen was quickest in first practice yesterday, with the Ferrari of Charles Leclerc fastest in second practice. Earlier today, championship leader Antonelli was nearly three tenths clear of the field in third practice. Mercedes, 160 points clear at the top of the constructors’ standings, have brought significant upgrades this weekend, which includes a new floor, rear suspension and rear corner. It is the team’s first significant car update since the Canadian Grand at the end of May.

This race in Malaysia represents the second leg of the season’s first flyaway triple header, with the Singapore Grand Prix to come next weekend, so the demands on the teams and the drivers are incredibly high. Qualifying from Sepang gets under way at 9am (GMT).

#1512. Liverpool played like a team fighting for their manager, but Pierre Sage looks like a dead man walking, writes LEWIS STEELE - as Reds clinch morale-boosting win at sorry Crystal Palace

Published: 11:14 EST, 8 November 2026 | Updated: 13:00 EST, 8 November 2026

By this time of the season, spirited performances mean little if you don't have the results to go with it.

Pierre Sage, who was sacked at Lyon two years ago, knows as much as anyone that this is a results-based business.

And he simply has not had enough results. Despite having Liverpool on the ropes at times here, Crystal Palace failed to land a knockout blow and that could be that for their under-fire manager, who looked like a dead man walking when he trudged off the pitch at full-time with a face like thunder.

Former Lens over-achiever Sage now seems set for a stuffing six weeks before Christmas and though he may curse at the small margins that denied his team a chance of a heavyweight and potential job-saving scalp here, the boss knows two wins in 10 league games is not good enough.

Liverpool, meanwhile, had the width of the crossbar and a throwback performance from goalkeeper Alisson to thank. In contrast to Sage, Andoni Iraola's side showed grit and determination to win when far from their best.

Alexis Mac Allister, Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak all scored as the Reds put a tough week behind them that saw them lose back-to-back games for the first time in the Iraola era, which prompted a chorus of the old terrace classic 'Poetry in Motion'.

Florian Wirtz scored a rare Liverpool as they won 3-1 at Crystal Palace in the Premier League

Wirtz scored Liverpool's second on 54 minutes as they ran out as 3-1 winners at Selhurst Park

Things are looking ominous for under-pressure Palace manager Pierre Sage after another loss

This performance was hardly William Wordsworth levels of poetry and Liverpool were far from on song during large swathes of this match but when it really mattered, the attackers demonstrated just why the club spent so much money on them.

CRYSTAL PALACE (3-4-2-1): Henderson 5; Lerma 6, Richards 6, Disasi 5; Mingueza 6 (Khalali 87), Wharton 5, Timber 6 (Timber 60, 6), Mitchell 6; Kamada 6, Pino 7 (McNeil 87); Larsen 5 (Nketiah 72, 7)

Subs not used: Benitez, Canvot, Chilwell, Doucoure, Hughes

LIVERPOOL (4-2-3-1): Alisson 9; Araujo 7 (Gomez 90), Jacquet 6, Van Dijk 6, Kerkez 6; Szoboszlai 7 (Nyoni 69, 7), Mac Allister 8; Gakpo 6 (Ngumoha 76) Wirtz 8, Barcola 7 (Munoz 69, 7); Isak 7 (Koumas 90)

Subs not used: Mamardashvili, Endo, McConnell, Tsimikas

Booked: Araujo, Barcola, Munoz, Mac Allister

Scorers: Mac Allister 40, Wirtz 54, Isak 89

Mac Allister resumed his bemusing role of the team's best aerial threat despite being their smallest player, Wirtz got a goal and assist, while Isak made it eight for the season to continue his prolific streak.

Bradley Barcola, meanwhile, proved what an asset he is despite a wasteful first half.

Those attackers were worthy of praise but no one deserved plaudits more so than goalkeeper, Alisson, who was player of the match in an illustration of Palace's first-half supremacy.

'I'm very pleased with Alisson's performance,' said Iraola. 'He has commanded the box very well and in games here a lot of things are normally happening in the boxes. He has shown the level he has for us. Overall we are getting good results away from home at difficult stadiums.'

The Brazilian is in the last year of his contract but put in his best performance for 18 months, dating back to a 1-0 win at Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League knockouts. He will not go on international duty and instead rest up after an injury-hit few years.

He denied Adam Wharton with a glancing header, thwarted Daichi Kamada with a fierce shot and then tipped round Quenten Timber's effort from distance. Palace also rattled the bar through Yeremy Pino in a first half that really should have ended up differently.

Jorgen Strand Larsen also had the ball in the net but was offside.

As it was, though, Liverpool were the team to take their chance when it came after a period of dilly-dallying and playing the wrong ball, guilty again of indecisiveness similar to the flaws shown against Arsenal last weekend and in the 3-2 defeat at Fenerbahce in midweek.

Liverpool led on 40 minutes when Alexis Mac Allister (centre left) scored from close range

The Argentine celebrates after breaking the deadlock for the Reds in the Premier League clash

Crystal Palace manager Pierre Sage is facing the sack after his side dropped to the bottom of the Premier League.

Palace have won just two of their ten league matches this season, with Sunday's 3-1 defeat to Liverpool leaving them at the foot of the league for the first time in nearly nine years.

Sage is expected to lose his job during the international break, with Sean Dyche and Thomas Frank leading the race to replace the French coach.

However, Sage believes his side have been unlucky with results this season and has requested the hierarchy remain patient.

The 47-year-old, who left RC Lens for Palace in the summer to succeed Oliver Glasner, also admitted the Palace squad needs strengthening - perhaps to absolve himself of some blame.

'You can create the links between these two things,' Sage replied when asked whether being bottom of the league heading into the international break could see him sacked.

'But a lot of times I've said we deserved better and it was the case again on Sunday.

'My job is not the most important thing, as I always said from the beginning. The most important thing is to find an efficient solution for the team and for the club.

'I know how important it is for the club to stay in the Premier League. The club just have to believe in that, and if it's not the case, they will take a decision.

'I always have confidence in myself because it's a big, big mistake to not be 100% involved in what I have to do.

'We have to adjust some positions during the winter transfer window to give more solutions and more efficiency and I think it will be okay.'

Mac Allister was the scorer as he continued a fine resurgence this season, with Dominik Szoboszlai the supplier after a week where he too had been criticised. The Hungarian whipped a cross towards Mac Allister, which was glanced past Henderson for 1-0.

The former Brighton player ran straight towards the Palace fans behind the goal and taunted the supporters that were once his rivals on the south coast.

Liverpool weathered another storm at the start of the second half and soon found themselves two up. Barcola, who had left lots to be desired in the first half, swapped wings at the break and made his first attack count.

The Frenchman put the after-burners on and motored down the pitch before feeding Wirtz, who composed himself and passed into the net for 2-0. Iraola praised the run of Isak which took him away from the ball but dragged defenders with him to create space for his colleague.

Isak squandered a one-versus-one chance not long after but was not going to miss another one minutes later, when a blisteringly quick counter-attack was started by Trey Nyoni and ended with Wirtz feeding Isak, who skipped past Chris Richards and finished calmly.

The three goals will delight the hierarchy, with all three of the £100m boys – Isak, Barcola and Wirtz – registering at least one goal or assist apiece, one each in Wirtz's case.

Alexander Isak scored the visitors' third in the 89th-minute with this right-footed finish

Eddie Nketiah pulled one back for Palace from the penalty in second-half stoppage time

This victory would not have been possible, though, without Alisson, now 34 and in the final year of his deal. For all the attacking talent at Iraola's disposal, the Basque will be delighted at his team's defensive determination when under the kosh here as Palace had 10 first-half shots.

Iraola knows his team has flaws and they remain a work-in-progress. But despite a few challenging afternoons, they appear to be heading in the right direction.

The same cannot be said for Sage, whose side pulled one back in stoppage time through an Eddie Nketiah penalty after Milos Kerkez committed a careless foul.

Palace were unlucky in this game but the cold, hard truth is that the recent FA Cup and Europa Conference League triumphs feel a world away now as they enter the international break rock bottom of the Premier League.

West Ham also won a European trophy in the last five years and look where they ended up — that should set alarm bells ringing that no success lasts for ever and Palace are not too big for relegation.

Nketiah's goal felt like it was too little, too late and the sage advice for Palace supremo Steve Parish might be a reluctant change in the dugout.

#1510. Can you name Italy’s victorious XI from the 2006 World Cup final?

Italy won their fourth World Cup title in 2006 – but can you name the starting XI from their victory over France in the final?

The 2006 World Cup probably isn’t best remembered for free-flowing football and nothing defined the tournament quite like the final in Berlin’s iconic Olympiastadion.

Both teams were unexpected finalists. Italy had squeezed past Australia before eliminating hosts Germany during a fine semi-final.

While France had dispatched Spain, Brazil and Portugal thanks largely to the majesty of Zinedine Zidane.

After trading a pair of early goals, both sides settled down for a two-hour arm wrestle that grew with tension with every passing minute.

Everybody remembers Zinedine Zidane’s headbutt and Italy going on to win the subsequent penalty shoot-out but how many of Italy’s starting XI can you name?

Marcello Lippi made full use of his squad during the competition and the XI that started the victory over France was a mix of generational talent and some more obscure Serie A players that became national heroes during the summer of 2006.

#1509. Roma to extend De Roon’s contract until 2028

Marten de Roon and Roma, a story that could continue beyond this season.

Arrived in the summer from Atalanta, the Dutch midfielder quickly demonstrated his potential as a valuable asset for Gasperini.

His performances on the pitch have been positive, both technically and physically. And so, despite turning 36 in March, discussions are already underway at Trigoria regarding a contract renewal.

According to Corriere dello Sport, the club intends to keep the former Atalanta captain, provided he continues to perform as expected and remains eager to play.

This doesn’t seem to be a problem at the moment. De Roon, however, prefers to take things one day at a time, without planning too far ahead: feeling good and maintaining his motivation remain his top priorities.

Gian Piero Gasperini, above all, is further strengthening the relationship with Roma. The bond between the two goes far beyond that of coach and player, so much so that the Dutchman could even join the coaching staff in the future. This possibility is still far from being finalized, but it speaks to their mutual respect. After all, De Roon himself acknowledged how much Gasperini has changed his “life and career.”

Financial considerations won’t be an obstacle.

They weren’t three months ago, when the coach personally called De Roon to convince him to follow him to the capital, and they shouldn’t be, even if he renews his contract. Roma wants to continue to rely on his experience, while the midfielder is focused solely on staying healthy and making himself useful. There will be time for the future, perhaps once again alongside Gasperini.

#1507. Pierre Sage sack: The Crystal Palace players who declined most in his reign

Crystal Palace just haven’t been the same since Oliver Glasner left and Pierre Sage arrived in his place in the dugout.

Palace had high hopes for Sage after seeing him guide Lens to second place in Ligue 1 last season. But Glasner was always going to be a tough act to follow after winning the FA Cup, Community Shield and Conference League during his reign. Not bad for a club without any major trophies before.

And Sage just hasn’t been up to scratch at Selhurst Park. A run of four defeats in a row in the Premier League, which started with a 5-0 thrashing by rivals Brighton, has seen Palace sink to the bottom of the Premier League.

They’ve also been unable to add to their opening-game win in the Europa League, most recently requiring a stoppage-time equaliser to salvage a draw against Hoffenheim.

The outlook has become bleak for Palace and they have been left with little choice but to sack Sage and move on. He would have wanted more than 16 games to try and get his project up and running, but there haven’t been enough convincing signs to stick with him.

Palace’s downturn in fortunes can be seen by how some of their players have regressed this season.

Here are the 10 Palace players whose ratings on WhoScored (from their Premier League appearances only) have decreased the most this season compared to last.

Bit unfair for Benitez to be top of the list, since he only played once in the league last season.

He got a 7.2 rating for that outing, but hasn’t got near that benchmark in any of his five league appearances so far this season.

You’d be forgiven for suspecting Mateta might have downed tools. Remember him trying to leave Palace by arguing the last year of his contract was invalid?

No player scored more for Palace under Glasner than Mateta, but he’s yet to get off the mark in the league this season.

A hamstring injury didn’t help, to be fair, and nor will a suspension after a red card against Spurs.

Not exactly the kind of reaction Palace were hoping for from Sarr after denying him the chance to join Liverpool this summer.

Last season was arguably the best of the winger’s career so far, but he’s been battling injuries this season and has only come off the bench twice in the league.

That’s not given him much time to build up good ratings, to be fair, but it’s definitely been a blow for Palace not to be able to rely on his impact.

Palace’s decision to take Guessand on loan again from Aston Villa raised some eyebrows after they neglected the chance to make his move permanent at first.

He’s only played twice as a sub since in the league and hasn’t scored.

The 31-year-old had the joint-busiest season of his career last time out, but has only played four times off the bench in the league this season at an average of 10 minutes a time.

He’s the lowest-rated Palace player who was there last season.

We wonder if the big clubs so often tipped to sign Wharton might be having some doubts about him now.

There’s ample time for the 22-year-old to turn this around, but after a summer in which he was left out of England’s World Cup squad, he risks getting left further behind.

Still only 20, Canvot has seen some of his more experienced defensive colleagues make way over the past couple of transfer windows.

He’s now one of the more important centre-backs left standing, but will need to make sure he reflects that responsibility with his performances going forward.

It’s a similar story for Richards, 26 and now in his fifth Premier League season.

As Palace’s only ever-present player in the league this term, he’s been part of some substantial defeats.

It’s not been a total disaster, though; he’s Palace’s fourth highest-rated player at the moment.

Riad is yet to really get up and running with Palace, despite this now being his third season with the club. Injuries haven’t helped.

He only played once in the league under Sage before doing his ACL.

After scoring once, Nketiah is halfway to matching his goal tally in the league from last season. Not great for a striker, is it?

He’s already started more league games than last season, but is fast becoming a source of frustration for Palace fans.

#1503. Winning is the only thing that matters to Rangers midfielder Dan Neil as Ibrox club continue to gain momentum in title challenge

Published: 13:52 EST, 8 November 2026 | Updated: 14:02 EST, 8 November 2026

Rangers midfielder Dan Neil admits he couldn’t care less about how his side go about picking up points as long as the wins keep coming.

The stand-in captain netted the crucial second in Saturday’s hard-fought victory over St Mirren in Paisley after Ryan Naderi had given the visitors a first-half lead from the penalty spot.

It was a result which extended Rangers’ unbeaten run to 12 in all competitions as they continue to build momentum following an unconvincing start to the campaign, and Neil insists that’s the only thing that matters at this stage.

He said: ‘I think every good team just finds a way to win.

‘Obviously, we’d like to win by four or five goals every single week but unfortunately that’s just not football. I do think it’s an area that we can improve on.

‘There’s been too many games this year where maybe we don’t get that second goal and it’s a bit nervy. Teams get a little bit of confidence off that and the momentum shifts.

Dan Neil savours the moment after putting the seal on Rangers' win with the second goal

‘I think it’s definitely something that we can improve on, putting teams to bed when we do go 1-0 up and go 1-0 up early doors when we’re creating chances.

‘But at the same time, finding a way to win is the most important way and whether that’s 1-0 or 5-0, at the end of the day it’s three points.’

While Rangers weren’t quite at their best in Paisley, they did more than enough to halt their poor recent run away from home.

Back-to-back 2-2 draws at Dundee and Hearts last month saw valuable points dropped in what is shaping up to be a tight title race, and Neil was delighted to get back to winning ways ahead of the international break.

‘The last two away results and performances really haven’t been us,’ said the former Sunderland man. ‘It was important that we didn’t have another one of them going into the break and have it lingering over us. Everyone played their part in making it a comfortable result.

‘Coming away from home in any league is tough, but especially this league. It’s important that the mentality of the group is right, which it is, and I think you’ve seen that on Saturday night.

‘It was important to put that hoodoo of those two results behind us and make sure that we win the game. I think there was some good football played for the majority of the game and we also dug in when we had to. That’s credit to every single player in that dressing room.’

#1499. Where are they now? The first Man Utd XI to face a Pochettino team

Manchester United are turning to a familiar former foe as their next manager, with Mauricio Pochettino replacing Michael Carrick in the hotseat.

It’s been a long time coming. Pochettino has been linked with the United job for years, but it’s never materialised. Until now.

Pochettino has been around in the Premier League long enough that he’s even managed a game against Sir Alex Ferguson, the legend that United have found it so hard to replace since his retirement 13 years ago.

It was in fact just Pochettino’s second game in charge of Southampton after being appointed in January 2013. His first, ironically, had been against an Everton side managed by Ferguson’s first successor, David Moyes.

After drawing with Everton, Pochettino suffered his first defeat at Old Trafford, despite Jay Rodriguez putting the visitors ahead within three minutes.

A brace from Wayne Rooney later in the first half turned it around to give United a 2-1 win.

But things would get better for Pochettino and he would leave an impression on Ferguson, who is believed to be one of his big backers.

Now, Pochettino is finally ready to get to work as the new United manager. But what has happened to the United players that were his opponents on his first visit to Old Trafford?

This is the starting XI Ferguson picked for his only ever clash with Pochettino and where they are now.

De Gea was midway through his second season with United at the time of Pochettino’s visit with Southampton. The first season hadn’t been plain sailing for the Spanish keeper, but he ultimately stood the test of time.

After leaving United in 2023 and spending a season as a free agent, De Gea joined Fiorentina in 2024, where he’s still playing now at the age of 36.

De Gea became Fiorentina’s captain last December. Just like current United keeper Senne Lammens, he hasn’t kept a clean sheet in any of his league games this season.

Like De Gea, Jones was in his second season at Old Trafford in 2012-13. He also stuck around until 2023, but his involvement in the later years of that spell was much more limited.

What might have been without injuries? We’ll never know. He had to retire at a relatively young age – he was only 30 when he played his last game – before transitioning into coaching.

Currently, Jones is a first-team coach with Sheffield United, forming part of Chris Wilder’s backroom staff. He’s previously coached in the Man Utd academy and with Blackburn Rovers.

Vidic has been retired for 10 years now, finishing his career with 18 months at Inter after all his United exploits.

He has had his UEFA Pro Licence coaching badge since 2018, but is yet to become a manager. He’s instead spent time investing in real estate and also enrolled on a UEFA course five years ago about executive management off the pitch.

Smalling signed for Porto in September on a free transfer after two years in Saudi Arabia. Love that for him, to be fair.

He had his highs and lows with United before becoming a force to be reckoned with in his career twilight with Roma.

Soon turning 37, Smalling made his Porto debut in a Portuguese cup match in October, but hasn’t played in the league yet.

Evra retired in 2019, a year after a short stint with West Ham. He’d last played for Man Utd in 2014 but went on to do some coaching with their academy while working through his badges.

He gets up to all sorts these days as an investor and public speaker. For example, he helped co-found the PLAYER app, which aims to connect people in football.

Anderson’s career ended in 2020, five years after he left United. However, he’s since turned out for United’s Legends team on the odd occasion.

The man making way for Pochettino, Carrick got his marching orders after United went into the international break in the relegation zone.

But the table across his full reign doesn’t look nearly as bad.

We’ve got a lot of time for Welbeck. Every time you think he’s down and out in his career, he bounces back.

The attacker left United in 2014 to join Arsenal, where he spent five years before joining Watford.

Welbeck eventually settled at Brighton and hit double figures of goals in each of the last two seasons there, earning him a surprise summer move to Chelsea.

The 35-year-old has come off the bench seven times in the league for Chelsea, as well as starting once, and scored three from three in the EFL Cup.

Recently crowned Pundit of the Year at the Broadcast Sport Awards – not just for saying what we all thought about the World Cup final’s half-time show – Rooney seems to be finding his calling after some unsuccessful stints as a manager.

And now he’s getting ready to go into the jungle.

Bet you didn’t know this guy’s still playing.

It never quite worked out for Kagawa at Old Trafford and so he retraced his steps back to Borussia Dortmund after just two years in England.

Spells with Besiktas, Real Zaragoza, PAOK and Sint-Truiden followed before he went back to Japan with Cerezo Osaka in 2023.

Kagawa originally started his career there before coming to Europe with Dortmund. Now 37, he has 12 J1 League appearances to his name this season.

Another former United player to have tested himself as a manager, Van Persie was in charge of Feyenoord until the summer.

He led them to second place in the Eredivisie last season, which was his first full campaign in charge.

He’s also previously managed Heerenveen, but has been doing some ambassadorial work while waiting for his next managerial role.

#1497. Xavi praises Malen: “He’s in excellent form. I can’t wait to see him on the pitch.”

Donyell Malen wants to take over the Netherlands.

A spark has been struck with Gian Piero Gasperini, and the number 14 seems unstoppable for the Giallorossi.

However, the situation is different for the national team. He struggled at the World Cup, and now Xavi must work to get him to perform at his best.

After missing for the September international break, the Spanish coach can count on the in-form center forward for the upcoming Nations League matches. Tomorrow (September 13), against Greece, the 1999-born player will play for the first time under the guidance of the former Barcelona midfielder.

At the press conference, Xavi praised Malen: “He’s training really well and is in excellent shape. He’s shown he’s perfectly at ease. He wants to show his potential. He’s giving his best in Italy. I’m trying to give him confidence because he can become important for the team.”

The former midfielder is eager to see ‘Bobby’ in action: “He has the ability to shine, create chances, be the right man, and then attack the goal at the same time. So, yes, he’s truly a player with many qualities that strengthen our team, and I can’t wait to see him on the pitch.”

#1496. South Korean star Kim Min-su has no goals and no assists, but it's no problem for Rangers boss Derek McInnes

Published: 14:24 EST, 8 November 2026 | Updated: 14:24 EST, 8 November 2026

Kim Min-su’s stat sheet since making the big-money move to Rangers over the summer should be the kind of thing that makes a manager legitimately wonder if both he and the club have been taken for a ride.

Twelve games, zero goals, zero assists. A rank-rotten return, on the face of it. So why does Derek McInnes not seem even remotely concerned by the whole palaver?

Well, simply put, he has a set of eyes. He, like everyone else, can clearly see that the South Korean is the heartbeat of everything that has been good about Rangers in an attacking sense ever since he was thrown into the team – even if the numbers don’t quite back it up.

It was the same story in yesterday’s hard-fought – but deserved – 2-0 win away at St Mirren.

It was hard to keep track of the number of times Min-su drifted in from the left-hand side to pick up possession with no opposition player within five yards. That’s not luck, it’s intelligence.

There is nobody playing in Scotland’s top flight more adept at taking the ball on the turn and driving into space either.

South Korean Kim Min-su contributes to all that is good about Rangers' attacking work

Min-su made life difficult for St Mirren during Rangers' 2-0 victory over the Paisley side

Dan Neil scores Rangers' second in a win that keeps them within four points of leaders Celtic

St Mirren couldn’t get near him for the majority of the first hour. They aren’t the first side to experience such difficulties, and they won’t be the last.

In full flight, he is a joy to watch operating in that pocket between the opposition midfield and defence.

It’s the bit after that where things start to become a little trickier for the talented 20-year-old.

He squandered a couple of opportunities to open his account here. The first came after playing a neat one-two with James Penrice late in the first half, with the ball sitting up perfectly for him ten yards out to smash home.

The choice to take one touch too many allowed Declan John to clear the danger.

So much of his game is based on instinct. Indeed, it’s a big part of what makes him such captivating viewing. But his decision-making in front of goal needs a lot of work.

Perhaps he’s guilty of overthinking things too much.

His manager certainly thinks so, admitting post-match that he felt Min-su was becoming ‘obsessed’ with registering his first goal for the club. In key moments, that shows.

A heavy touch early in the second period after being played in by Badredine Bouanani – unusually quiet here on the right – once again suggested he is feeling the pressure.

But let’s not forget, he’s essentially a kid trying to find his feet in a new country, and in a league which couldn’t be more different in terms of speed and style from what he was used to in Spain.

That he has actually managed to settle in so seamlessly should be applauded. It can’t have been an easy transition but he has quickly endeared himself to the supporters.

It’s why they are every bit as desperate as the player himself to get the monkey off his back.

They needn’t worry. If he keeps doing what he’s doing, the goals will come. Of that there is no doubt.

Some context has to be attached to his failure to notch an assist too. It’s a misleading stat, given that it depends entirely on someone else putting the ball away when it counts.

Min-su created multiple chances for his team-mates in Paisley, the best of which saw Kevin Kelsy put through on goal. It’s hardly his fault that the big man fluffed his lines. The Venezuelan has been in good form but had a stinker here.

At some point, everything will come together for Min-su. And it’s not as if he didn’t have an impact in both of Rangers’ goals against St Mirren.

It may have gone unnoticed amongst everything else, but he absolutely busted a gut to get himself into the box in the build-up to Dan Neil’s deflected strike which sealed the points on 61 minutes. That willingness to put the hard yards in off the ball is every bit as impressive as his ability on it.

And it was his pass to Penrice which led to the full-back being clipped by Samuel Ramos inside the box to give Rangers the opportunity to go ahead from the penalty spot early in the first half.

In truth, they may have been a little fortunate to do so. Put it this way, had referee Nick Walsh not given it, there’s not a chance in hell that VAR would have got involved.

Ryan Naderi stepped up to slot into the bottom corner to take his tally to nine for the season in all competitions.

It says a lot about where Naderi's head is that he had the confidence to do so, especially after blowing a great chance from six yards out only moments before. The German-born Czech international is a changed man, all right.

Speaking of confidence, there is no shortage of it at the other end of the park either. At times, the defensive pairing of Olwethu Makhanya and Emmanuel Fernandez look like they’re playing five-a-sides.

It’s usually the latter who throws in the odd lapse of concentration to add some peril to proceedings, but yesterday it was the normally dependable Makhanya’s turn to give his manager a few hairy moments. Thankfully for the South African, St Mirren couldn’t take advantage.

Craig McLeish’s men could have no complaints over the final result but could have made things interesting late on had either Eseosa Sule or Calvin Ramsay finished from close range.

It’s now just one win in nine for the Buddies, who – much like last season – just can’t seem to put the ball in the back of the net consistently. That problem plagued them so much that they ended up in the relegation play-off spot last year.

McLeish has done an excellent job since taking over from Stephen Robinson. A far better one than anyone could have possibly predicted. He has changed the style of this team completely in a very short space of time and so you have to trust he will be able to find a solution to their goalscoring issues too.

Rangers might be 13 points better off but they head into the international break also in search of that perfect balance.

When they’re on it, they’re very good. But they are still not commanding games from start to finish with any sort of regularity.

They won’t necessarily have to be pleasing on the eye to end up with their hands on the Premiership trophy come May. Celtic’s triumph last season proved that.

The Rangers supporters will gladly put up with imperfect displays for the next six months if that’s going to be the end result.

And if the likes of Min-su can hit the goal trail sometime soon, there’s a decent chance that’s exactly how things will play out.

#1495. Alejandro Balde gives priority to Roma move

Roma will be very active in the transfer market in January. Gian Piero Gasperini has primarily requested offensive reinforcements, but the Giallorossi continue to monitor Alejandro Balde.

The Spaniard is finding less and less space at Barcelona, ​​and his departure in January is increasingly likely.

Roma is delighted by some news from Spain: according to Spanish newspaper Sport, the 2003-born player has put the Roman club at the top of his list of options should he leave Camp Nou. Negotiations between the clubs, however, are an uphill battle.

Roma and Barcelona are struggling to find a formula that everyone can agree on; the clubs will continue to work until January to find a compromise. Balde’s salary is also a problem: approximately €5.5 million net is beyond the reach of the Trigoria club.

The deal could be finalized by someone who helped the Roman club close a deal this summer. After Rodrigo Mora, Jorge Mendes could also intervene to bring the 2003-born player to the capital. All discussions are postponed: the Giallorossi have other priorities.
